papers.title: High‐Conductivity Active Interface Layer for Active Lithium Reservoir in Micro‐Silicon‐Based All‐Solid‐State Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Sulfide‐based all‐solid‐state lithium‐ion batteries (ASSLIBs) employing fully active, carbon‐free micro‐silicon (µSi) anodes present significant potential for high energy density, enhanced safety, and reduced cost. However, their practical application is challenged by inherent issues such as sluggish reaction kinetics, substantial volume expansion, and low Coulombic efficiency, which collectively degrade overall electrochemical performance. Herein, an interfacial engineering strategy is developed to construct an active interface layer on µSi particles via a mechanochemical cold‐pressing method. The resulting Li─Si alloy layer acts as an active lithium reservoir, which enables active lithium reservoir. Furthermore, this spontaneously formed active layer exhibits high ionic/electronic conductivities and accommodates volume changes due to its favorable mechanical properties, thereby improving electrode reaction kinetics and structural stability. ASSLIBs fabricated with LiNi 0.83 Co 0.12 Mn 0.05 O 2 cathode and modified µSi anode deliver a high initial specific capacity of 182.55 mAh g −1 and retain a capacity retention of 89.2% after 200 cycles at 0.1 C. This work offers a facile interfacial engineering technique for constructing self‐compensating lithium reservoirs and promotes the development of high‐energy‐density silicon‐based solid‐state batteries.

papers.title: Formulating the Dual‐Function Separator‐Enabled Homogenizing Ion Flux in Nonflammable Phosphate toward High Stable Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The high‐energy lithium metal battery employing a nonflammable phosphate electrolyte is an attractive strategy to resolve the notorious safety trouble. Unfortunately, the sluggish ion dissociation and transport kinetics, strong interaction of Li + ‐phosphates, and uncontrollable secondary reaction between the electrode and electrolyte interfaces severely impedes the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries. Herein, the dual‐function separators with fast ion dissociation and transport capability are designed to enable the homogeneous and efficient ion flux in nonflammable phosphate electrolyte. By virtue of the regulating effect of the designed dual‐function separator, the homogeneous distribution of the ion field and electric field are constructed, thus reducing the concentration polarization among nonflammable phosphate electrolyte and weakening the parasitic reaction of the metallic lithium anode and nickel‐rich cathode with the electrolyte. The Li||Li symmetrical cells exhibit remarkable cycling stability of above 1000 h at 2 mA cm −2 . Moreover, the Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) battery exhibits above 90% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 1C. Furthermore, stable bidirectional electrode‐electrolyte interfaces are also realized after cycling. This approach holds great promise for regulating the ion flux in nonflammable electrolyte, and would encourage more separator engineering design to optimize ionic transport behavior.

papers.title: Fluorine‐Rich Lewis Acidic MOF as Ion Modulator to Enable Dendrite‐Free Li Plating for Ah‐Level Li‐Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium metal stands as the most promising anode material to drive the development of next‐generation energy storage systems owing to its unparalleled theoretical gravimetric capacity. However, the naturally formed solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) is inadequate to suppress the uncontrolled growth of lithium dendrites, posing the safety concerns for lithium metal batteries (LMBs). Herein, we propose a F‐rich Lewis acid metal‐organic framework (F‐mof) as an anion captor and a cation accelerator to mitigate the concentration polarization and expedite the lithium ion transport at anode‐electrolyte interface. The lithiophilic nature of F‐mof with a 3D open framework facilitates the uniform lithium deposition and mitigates the electrode volume change during extended cycling. This strong Lewis acid‐modified Li anode enables Li||Li symmetric cells to achieve an extended cycle life of 2000 h at a high capacity of 2 mAh cm −2 . The modified LMBs with LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cathodes demonstrate the prolonged 700 cycles at 1 C. The NCM811‐pouch cells with a thick cathode (30 mg cm −2 ) achieve a high energy density of 300 Wh kg −1 based on entire pouch weight. Moreover, this work uses a conversion‐type FeF 3 cathode to assemble multilayer pouch cell, achieving a high capacity of 600 mAh for fluoride conversion reaction batteries.

papers.title: Diagnosis of Mechanisms of Kinetics in Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Cathode Materials
papers.abstract_en: Abstract The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. In this work, we establish a quantitative diagnostic method for the RDS in LRMOs using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at different states of charge (SOC) and C-rates. From our results, the SOC determines the intrinsic bottleneck of the RDS, while the C-rate drives the transition from single-step to mixed control. Upon discharging to 4.4 V, the RDS is dominated by electron transfer at the interface accompanied by layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas it is strongly influenced by solid-state diffusion in the bulk with depletion of Li vacancies arising from Jahn–Teller distortion when discharging to 3.0 V. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.
papers.summary_ko: 리튬 리치 망간계 산화물(LRMO) 양극재의 속도 결정 단계(RDS)를 정량적으로 진단하는 방법을 제시했다. in-situ 임피던스 분광법과 선형주사전위법을 이용해 분석한 결과, SOC는 RDS의 본질적 한계를 결정하고 C-rate는 단일 단계에서 혼합 제어로의 전환을 유도함을 확인했다. 4.4V 방전에서는 계면 전자전달이, 3.0V에서는 얀-텔러 왜곡에 의한 Li 공공 고갈에 따른 고체 확산이 RDS를 지배하며, 고율에서는 전하전달보다 Li+ 확산이 주된 요인임을 밝혔다.

papers.title: Carbonyl‐Rich Polyimide Covalent Organic Frameworks as Anode Coating for Uniform Sodium Deposition
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs), by virtue of their structural diversity, high specific surface area, and facile functionalization, have emerged as a promising anode coating for sodium metal batteries (SMBs). Herein, we report two polyimide COFs (TATT‐NTCDA‑COF and TATT‐PMDA‑COF) constructed from isocyanurate‐based amine building blocks, which feature profuse ion‐binding active sites and a robust, ordered framework, thereby significantly enhancing ion transport, fostering uniform sodium deposition, and suppressing dendrite growth. Benefiting from this unique design and its reliable stability, the symmetric cell based on TATT‐NTCDA‑COF operates stably for over 1200 h at 0.1 mA cm −2 . When assembled into a full cell with a commercial Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) cathode, it delivers an initial discharge capacity of 107.4 mAh g −1 , retains 9.3% capacity after 800 cycles at 1 C, and maintains over 90% capacity retention even after 1390 cycles at 5 C and 750 cycles at 10 C. Thus, the rational design of carbonyl‐rich 2D COFs is of great significance for the construction of artificial anode coatings for SMBs.

papers.title: Asymmetric Cooperative Solvation Structure Enables Entropy‐Enthalpy Compensation for Ultralow Temperature Sodium‐Metal and Sodium–Ion Pouch Cells
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Sodium‐metal batteries are promising for low‐temperature energy storage, yet conventional electrolytes suffer from an intrinsic trade‐off between thermodynamic stability and kinetic transport, causing salt precipitation and solvation collapse. Herein, an asymmetric cooperative solvation structure (ACSS) is introduced to spatially decouple these conflicting requirements via coordination competition between a strong solvating solvent (diethylene glycol dimethyl ether, DME) and a weak solvating (diethylene glycol diethyl ether, DEE). The DME‐rich inner core forms compact ternary coordination clusters with Na + and anions (PF 6 − /BF 4 − ), ensuring enthalpic stability and high salt solubility via geometric ion confinement, while the DEE‐rich outer shell sustains entropic mobility through rapid ligand exchange, facilitating hopping transport and lowering desolvation barriers. This enthalpy–entropy compensation preserves ionic conductivity and structural integrity below −40°C. High anion occupancy within the stable clusters promotes preferential anion reduction, yielding an inorganic‐rich SEI with high mechanical modulus and low Na + migration energy, effectively suppressing dendrite growth and interfacial polarization. Consequently, Na||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 94% at −40°C. Scaled‐up 1.2 Ah hard carbon||Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 P 2 O 7 and 1.2 Ah hard carbon||NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 pouch cells sustain 400 and 550 cycles at −30°C and −20°C, respectively, demonstrating the promising practical applicability of this electrolyte design.

papers.title: Anchored Fluoro‐Shielded Solvation for Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)‐based polymer electrolytes are promising candidates for solid‐state lithium metal batteries owing to their favorable overall electrochemical properties. However, conventional PVDF‐based polymer electrolytes suffer from uneven solvation distribution, discontinuous ion‐transport pathways, and unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces caused by residual solvents and porous PVDF frameworks. Herein, we report an anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation strategy to construct a high‐performance PVDF‐based polymer electrolyte. By integrating polyanionic anchoring sites with fluorinated shielding segments, the optimized electrolyte enables spatially distributed anion‐rich solvation pathways, homogeneous Li + transport, and robust LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). The polymer electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.26×10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.69, an oxidative onset potential of 5.27 V, and a critical current density of 6.4 mA cm −2 . Spectroscopic and interfacial analyses reveal that the anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation structure promotes LiF‐rich SEI formation and suppresses solvent decomposition. Consequently, Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 batteries retain 80.2% capacity after 2000 cycles under high‐voltage and high‐rate conditions of 4.5 V and 5 C. This work highlights anchored fluoro‐shielded solvation as an effective molecular design principle for advanced polymer electrolytes toward practical high‐voltage and high‐rate solid‐state Li metal batteries.

papers.title: Submolecular Selenium Enables Low‐Pressure and Recyclable All‐Solid‐State Li–Se Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐selenium (Li–Se) batteries offer high energy density and intrinsic safety, but their practical deployment is hindered by sluggish solid‐state redox kinetics, large volume fluctuations, and unstable solid‐solid interfaces, particularly under low stack pressure. Here we report a submolecular Se x cathode by converting crystalline cyclo‐Se 8 into amorphous single‐atom and short‐chain Se (Se x , x < 4) species anchored on graphene (Se x @G), which increases the electronic conductivity from 6.3 × 10 −5 to 13 S cm −1 and Li + diffusivity from 1.7 × 10 −14 to 2.0 × 10 −11 cm 2 s −1 . Meanwhile, a Li 2 O‐nanoshell‐modified sulfide solid electrolyte is designed to stabilize the interface against both Li metal and Se cathode. As a result, all‐solid‐state Li–Se batteries deliver the theoretical capacity of 673 mAh g −1 at 0.1 C and retain 86% capacity over 2800 cycles at 3 C under 8 MPa, with stable operation down to −30°C. All‐solid‐state Li–Se pouch cells further achieve an energy density of 420 Wh kg −1 and 94% capacity retention after 300 cycles under 2.5 MPa. Post‐mortem analysis reveals that the submolecular Se x species are not only structurally preserved but also recyclable after electrochemical cycling within the solid‐state reaction environment. This work establishes submolecular chalcogen chemistry as a new design paradigm for low‐pressure, recyclable, and high‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries.

papers.title: Stabilizing hydrogen bonds and engineering multi-component hetero-solvation architecture for dendrite-free zinc metal anodes
papers.abstract_en: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are promising candidates for renewable grid energy storage, but their development is limited by non-uniform zinc deposition, hydrogen evolution reactions (HERs), and byproduct growth at the zinc anode interface. Herein, a dual-regulation strategy integrating bulk solvation reorganization with interfacial dynamic electrostatic shielding is developed by introducing a trace amount of 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium iodide (BMIMI, BI) into a Zn(OTf) 2 aqueous electrolyte. Multi-dimensional microscopic spectra and quantitative molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the co-incorporation of BMIM + cations and I − anions establishes a diversified I − -H 2 O-OTf − hetero-primary solvation sheath, disrupting the chemical degradation pathways caused by free water aggregation. Due to its electrostatic adsorption energy advantage on multiple crystal planes, BMIM + preferentially occupies active sites to form a dynamic cation shielding field. This forces Zn 2+ to diffuse away smoothly from local tip protrusions and induces lateral planar epitaxial growth along the dense (002) preferred crystal plane. Consequently, the electrolyte shows stability within the fundamental potential window during cyclic voltammetry tests, and the interfacial desolvation energy barrier decreases from 51.29 to 23.28 kJ mol −1 . This affords the Zn//Cu battery a stable Coulombic efficiency of 99.74%, and the Zn//Zn symmetric battery achieves a lifespan exceeding 7500 h under variable loads and high areal capacities. In full-cell applications, the cell maintains a capacity retention of 84.07% after 5000 cycles at a high current density of 2 A g −1 . Combined with ex-situ distribution of relaxation times and dynamic impedance evolution, this strategy confirms the feasibility of the system for industrial-grade variable-load energy storage scenarios.

papers.title: Neutron Depth Profiling: The Core Link Connecting the Microscopic Mechanisms of Lithium‐Ion Batteries With Intelligent Design
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Neutron Depth Profiling (NDP) is a non‐destructive, in situ quantitative depth‐analysis technique underpinned by neutron‐induced nuclear reactions. Offering high 6 Li‐isotope sensitivity and nanometer‐to‐micrometer depth resolution, NDP delivers isotope‐resolved lithium spatial information hardly accessible via conventional probes including secondary‐ion mass spectrometry (SIMS), X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and operando neutron imaging, yet it suffers from depth‐dependent resolution degradation, limited lateral performance, and requires large‐scale neutron‐beam facilities. This paper systematically reviews NDP fundamentals, global neutron‐source progress, and cutting‐edge battery applications, covering lithium‐ion migration in electrodes, lithium dendrite nucleation and growth, and the “reversible short‐circuit” effect at solid‐electrolyte interfaces. The unique merit of NDP for quantitative 6 Li depth‐profiling is highlighted, while noting that NDP cannot independently resolve full‐element maps or nanoscale interfaces and demands complementary characterizations. A roadmap integrating NDP with multimodal measurements and physics‐informed machine learning for intelligent battery design is outlined, alongside open challenges: inversion non‐uniqueness under low‐signal conditions and translation from model cells to practical batteries. This work provides actionable guidelines to leverage NDP for bridging microscopic lithium mechanisms and rational design of next‑generation batteries with high safety and high energy density.

papers.title: Molecular design of sulfonate-graphene oxide frameworks (GOF) separators with crystallographic orientation and ion selectivity for high-rate zinc-ion storage
papers.abstract_en: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) are highly attractive for grid-scale energy storage owing to their inherent safety and low cost. However, Zn dendrite growth and parasitic side reactions severely limit their fast-charging capability and cycling stability. Graphene oxide (GO) is a promising separator scaffold since its layered, graphitic domains can template Zn deposition along the (002) plane. Concurrently, its abundant oxygen-containing functional groups enable the interlayer regions chemical expansion and functionalization. Herein, we report two strategies to tailor Janus separators, achieved by spray-coating sulfonate-containing GO frameworks (GOFs) onto commercial cellulose fiber (CF) membranes. The reaction of GO with two diamino-substituted disulfonic acid pillars, i.e. 2,5-diaminobenzene-1,4-disulfonic acid (S1) and 2,2′-benzidinedisulfonic acid (S2), yields a GO interlayer spacing expansion from 0.79 to 1.09 nm and 1.41 nm, respectively, opening selective Zn²⁺ transport channels. The pendant sulfonate groups within these channels lock Zn ions into (002) texture, electrostatically repel SO₄²⁻, and release H⁺, collectively suppressing parasitic side reactions and raising the Zn²⁺ transference number from 0.45 (CF) to 0.62 (GOF-S1@CF) and 0.68 (GOF-S2@CF). Zn//Zn symmetric cells assembled with the Janus separators cycle for 2700–3600 h at 2 mA cm⁻², compared with 1200 h for bare CF. Zn//MnO₂ full cells retain 81.2% of their capacity after 2000 cycles at 1 A g⁻¹, and a Zn//NH₄V₄O₁₀ pouch cell retains 82.4% capacity over 400 cycles, whereas the CF-based pouch cell fails within 20 cycles. These results demonstrate that combining ion-selective transport with crystallographic control of Zn deposition is an effective route to long-lived, fast-charging AZIB separators.

papers.title: Li+-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
papers.abstract_en: Conventional brain pacemakers rely on electrochemical batteries, which suffer from leakage, performance degradation, and neurotoxicity, posing serious safety risks. Ceramic-based pulse generators with ultra-fast discharge, high-temperature stability, and self-diagnostic capability offer a promising alternative. However, most dielectric ceramics lose their polarization activity at elevated temperatures. To address this challenge, we introduce a high-entropy composition design that induces a Li-locked domain effect in the ceramic system (1-x)[0.9(Bi0.47Na0.47Yb0.03Tm0.01)TiO3−0.1LiTaO3]−0.06(Ba0.3Sr0.7)(Sn0.5Hf0.5)O3. We demonstrate that Li+-enriched regions lock polar nanodomains, preserving them even at 300 °C. This mechanism yields a recoverable energy density of 11.43 J·cm−3, an efficiency of 84.67%, and excellent temperature stability (Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C). Moreover, Yb3+/Tm3+ co-doping enables anomalous thermal enhancement of photoluminescence and precise temperature monitoring. Remarkably, the experimentally measured temperature sensing deviation is only ±0.23 K. The integration of stable energy storage and optical self-diagnosis provides a new paradigm for ceramic-based brain pacemaker pulse generators with early warning capability, pointing toward a possible solution to the intrinsic safety limitations of conventional battery-powered devices. Dielectric energy-storage ceramics lose polarization at high temperatures, limiting harsh-environment use. Here, the authors show a Li+- locked domain effect in high-entropy BNT-based ceramics, achieving Wrec = 11.43 J cm−3, η = 84.67%, Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C, with self-diagnostic thermometry.

papers.title: From Order to Disorder: A Crystalline-Amorphous Core-Shell Structure Enables Superior Ionic Conductivity and Interfacial Stability in Halide Electrolytes
papers.abstract_en: Halide solid-state electrolytes are critical for developing high-safety, high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries. However, most existing synthesis methods for halide electrolytes rely on non-equilibrium strategies, which struggle to simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity and good stability. Here, we propose a facile one-step solid-state route that constructs a highly conductive and structurally robust crystalline-amorphous core-shell heterostructure by aliovalent doping of Hf 4+ /Zr 4+ into Li 3 YCl 6 . In this heterostructure, the ordered crystalline core serves as a robust scaffold, while nanocrystallites that simultaneously promote structural integrity and ion transport are embedded within the continuous, highly conductive amorphous shell. These structural features synergistically establish a three-dimensional ion migration network with low transport barriers and high connectivity, enabling Li 2.6 Y 0.6 Hf 0.4 Cl 6 to achieve a room-temperature ionic conductivity of 1.4 mS·cm −1 , a 37-fold enhancement over the pristine phase, and an activation energy of 0.30 eV. Benefiting from its excellent interfacial stability against Li–In anode, all-solid-state batteries employing the LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 cathode operate stably without a sulfide interlayer, achieving 80.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at room temperature and 73.8% retention after 100 high-rate cycles at elevated temperature. With an additional sulfide interlayer to further optimize the interface, the cell delivers a prolonged cycle life with 87.2% capacity retention over 580 cycles. Through a straightforward solid-state doping approach, this work designs a highly conductive and structurally stable halide electrolyte, offering a new design paradigm for halide electrolytes.

papers.title: Engineering a borate-rich interphase for highly stable all-solid-state sodium batteries
papers.abstract_en: Composite polymer electrolytes (CPEs) are promising for all-solid-state sodium batteries, yet interfacial instability limits their practical applications. The commonly used NaTFSI can electrochemically form an NaF–Na2CO3–Na2O-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) to regulate sodium-ion deposition, but the resulting protective layer still suffers from early failure. Herein, a boron-enriched interphase is introduced by incorporating NaDFOB into a polyethylene-oxide based CPE, enabling stable and dendrite-free Na plating/stripping. Experimental results reveal that DFOB− preferentially decomposes over TFSI−, forming an Na4B2O5–NaF–Na2CO3–Na2O SEI with synergistic ion-conductive and electron-blocking properties. Moreover, theoretical calculations are performed to investigate the synergistic ionic-enhanced and electronic-restricted capability of the SEI layer. Benefiting from the stabilized SEI, the Na||Na symmetric cell exhibits outstanding cyclic stability (5,000 h at 0.5 mA cm−2) and full cell delivers a high initial capacity of 99.4 mAh g−1 with 92.38% retention at 3 C after 9,000 cycles.

papers.title: Cross-modal topology decodes battery faults from sparse voltage snapshots
papers.abstract_en: Battery safety remains the primary bottleneck for mass electric vehicle (EV) adoption, yet field monitoring is hamstrung by a fundamental asymmetry: complex electrochemical faults must be diagnosed via sparse, low-frequency voltage measurements. Existing methods struggle to resolve the signal ambiguity between overlapping fault modes without hardware upgrades. Here, we demonstrate that these distinct fault fingerprints are not lost, but topologically folded within voltage snapshots. We introduce DeFault, a cross-modal diagnostic framework that mathematically unfolds one-dimensional voltage sequences into multi-dimensional phase-space topologies. DeFault employs a bidirectional cross-attention mechanism that acts as an autonomous, physics-aligned filter, explicitly decoding compounded fault modes that remain fundamentally invisible to sequence-based methods. Validated on a field dataset of 16.4 million data records from 99 in-service EVs, our method achieves an average accuracy of 0.96 and an F1 score of 0.84 for four fault types using only 500-second snapshots (spanning <100 mV). This work proves that high-fidelity, interpretable electrochemical diagnosis is achievable on legacy fleets without new sensors, providing a scalable solution for the battery safety crisis.

papers.title: Chemically Reactivatable Sulfide Interfaces for Low‐Pressure Thick‐Cathode Solid‐State Na–S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Low‐pressure solid‐state Na–S batteries with thick sulfur cathodes are attractive for high‐energy storage, but their operation is fundamentally constrained by the progressive loss of solid–solid contact during sulfur conversion. Once insulating sulfides become poorly connected to the electronic network, charge recovery becomes incomplete and cathode passivation rapidly accumulates. Here, we construct chemically reactivatable sulfide interfaces by embedding Fe 3 C–MnO heteropoints within nitrogen‐doped hollow carbon nanotubes. The heterointerface integrates carbon‐side electronic coupling, sulfide‐side affinity, and interfacial polarization, thereby suppressing localized sulfide accumulation and sustaining charge‐stage sulfur recovery as mechanical confinement weakens. This effect is strongly pressure dependent. Under high compression, the electrochemical responses of different hosts converge, whereas under contact‐limited conditions the Fe 3 C–MnO architecture preserves markedly higher sulfur utilization, lower polarization, and superior cycling stability. Consequently, the operational pressure required to retain ≥80% of the 10 MPa discharge capacity decreases from approximately 2 MPa for the control cathodes to 0.2 MPa for Fe 3 C–MnO/NC@S. A 200 µm cathode with 8.3 mg cm −2 sulfur sustains reversible cycling at 0.2 MPa, together with a pouch‐cell energy density of 696 Wh kg cathode −1 . These results establish sulfide‐interface reactivation as a route to decouple reversible sulfur chemistry from stringent mechanical confinement.

papers.title: Anion Packing and Li⁺ Coordination Topology in Ether-Functionalized Imidazolium Ionic-Liquid Electrolytes: FSI versus TFSI
papers.abstract_en: We ask how anion identity relates to L i + coordination and the transport penalty of lithium-salt addition in ether-functionalized [MOEmim] ionic liquids. [ MOEmim ] [ FSI ] , [ MOEmim ] [ TFSI ] and their matched Li-salt electrolytes ( x ( LiX ) = 0.167 ) were synthesized and studied by FTIR, rheometry, impedance spectroscopy, 25 ns polarizable molecular dynamics (APPLE&P) with atom-resolved coordination and Onsager transport analysis, and COSMO-RS. LiFSI more than doubles the viscosity of [ MOEmim ] [ FSI ] (21.3 → 52.4 mPa·s at 25°C), whereas LiTFSI raises that of [ MOEmim ] [ TFSI ] by only about 10%, though the FSI electrolyte remains the more conductive. Binding strength does not run in the direction required: COSMO-RS finds L i + coordination more favorable to TFS I − at every cluster size, by 11–29 kJ mol⁻¹. The difference lies in coordination topology. L i + holds a near-invariant oxygen coordination of 4.78–4.96, and the number of partners sharing it tracks anion size: 3.9 distinct anions alongside FS I − against 3.2 alongside TFS I − , so denticity follows arithmetically: 1.24 against 1.56. FSI aggregates are 1.7–1.8 × larger though non-percolating, and ether-oxygen coordination is a minority motif. The Li⁺ coordination topology and the transport penalty of salt addition therefore track anion packing, while ion correlations limit the fraction of the total ion motion that produces net charge transport. Because FSI⁻ and TFSI⁻ differ in more than volume, this identifies an operative packing explanation rather than isolating volume as an independent variable.

papers.title: Ultralow Deposition Potential and Antisite-Boosted Diffusivity of Li3Ga2 Anode for All-Solid-State Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Existing alloy anodes suffer from high redox potentials and sluggish Li atomic kinetics, limiting the energy density and rate capability of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Herein, we report a well-designed Li3Ga2 alloy anode that simultaneously delivers an ultralow Li deposition potential (0.007 V vs. Li+/Li) and fast Li atomic diffusion kinetics (2.0 × 10–8 cm2 s–1). The high Li atomic diffusivity primarily originates from moderate Li/Ga antisite mixing, stabilizing the anode-solid electrolyte interface and enabling a high critical current density of 24 mA cm–2 in ASSLBs. Coupled with a LiCoO2 cathode, the ASSLB delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 96.5% and an ultralong cycle life of 2000 cycles at room temperature, with a high output voltage of 3.84 V, outperforming state-of-the-art alloy-based counterparts. A practical all-solid-state pouch cell employing the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode also delivers outstanding cycling stability. This work redefines alloy anode design principles through synergistic optimization of Li deposition potential and Li atomic diffusivity.

papers.title: Scalable crosslinking-regulated membranes with ultra-high Li+/Mg2+ selectivity for lithium recovery from brines
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Membrane-based separation has emerged as a competitive technology for lithium extraction from salt-lake brines. However, its industrial implementation remains limited by the low Li + /Mg 2+ selectivity of conventional membranes. In this work, we demonstrate that regulation of the crosslinking degree during membrane formation enables subnanometer pore size control within the narrow window required for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Under electrodialysis conditions, the membrane achieved a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor of up to 6454 at an Mg/Li mass ratio of 140, outperforming previously reported membranes for Li + /Mg 2+ separation. Importantly, the membrane maintained a Li + /Mg 2+ separation factor above 1200 in untreated natural salt-lake brine, despite the high Mg/Li mass ratio (Mg/Li = 87) and the presence of multiple competing ions. Fabrication of a 25 cm × 35 cm membrane and stable performance over 15 days of repeated operation further supported the practical viability of this approach. The practical membrane design strategy reported in this work can inspire the development of ion-selective membranes with precisely regulated subnanometer pores for a wide range of sustainable separation processes.
papers.summary_ko: 가교 정도를 조절하여 서브나노미터 기공 크기를 정밀하게 제어한 분리막을 통해 염수에서 리튬을 추출하는 기술을 제시했다. 전기투석 조건에서 Li+/Mg2+ 분리 지수 최대 6454를 달성했으며, 실제 염호 염수에서도 1200 이상의 분리 성능을 유지했다. 25cm×35cm 크기의 분리막을 제작해 15일간 안정적으로 작동함을 입증하여 실용화 가능성을 보였다.

papers.title: HERC2–UBE3A structure uncovers a domain-motif protein network potentially altered in Angelman and related syndromes
papers.abstract_en: UBE3A and HERC2 are two mutually interacting HECT E3 Ubiquitin ligases whose genes are altered in 15q11.2-13.1 Duplication (Dup15q) Syndrome, Angelman Syndrome (AS) and other phenotypically-related mental retardation syndromes. Using quantitative binding assays, X-ray crystallography and sequence conservation analysis, we characterize the core interface of the HERC2-UBE3A complex, involving the RLD2 domain of HERC2 and a “DxDKDxD” sequence from a disordered region of UBE3A. The sequence determinants of the interface are conserved in numerous animals with a central nervous system. HERC2 also binds similar DxDKDxD motifs within a handful of other proteins relevant to brain development (DOCK10, PCM1, USP35, BAZ2B, ARID4A, ARIP4, RERE and MYT1). We further investigate the interaction of HERC2 with DOCK10, a RAC1- and CDC42-GEF protein that regulates dendritic spine morphogenesis in hippocampal neurons. siRNA-mediated knockdown of HERC2 affects the GEF activity of DOCK10, and mutagenesis of the HERC2-binding motif in DOCK10 disrupts both its GEF activity and its ability to drive dendritic spine formation. In developing brains, an abnormal dosage of either HERC2 or its dominant partner UBE3A may thus alter the proportions of RLD2-mediated complexes, including HERC2-DOCK10, and may thereby perturb dendritic spine morphogenesis and neurodevelopment. UBE3A and HERC2 are two interacting HECT E3 ligases altered in Angelman and related neurodevelopmental syndromes. Here the authors show UBE3A to bind HERC2 via a “DxDKDxD” motif found in nine additional HERC2-binding brain proteins, suggesting a HERC2-centered network relevant for neurodevelopment.
papers.summary_ko: UBE3A와 HERC2 두 E3 유비퀴틴 리가아제 간의 상호작용 구조를 규명한 연구로, Angelman 증후군 등 신경발달 질환과 관련된 도메인-모티프 결합 네트워크를 밝혔다. HERC2의 RLD2 도메인이 UBE3A 및 DOCK10 등 여러 단백질의 "DxDKDxD" 서열과 결합함을 확인했으며, HERC2 결손이 DOCK10의 GEF 활성과 수상돌기 가시 형성에 영향을 미침을 보였다. 이는 HERC2/UBE3A 발현량 이상이 신경발달 과정을 교란할 수 있음을 시사한다.

papers.title: Fine-Tuning Universal Machine Learning Potentials Enables Efficient Computation of Li Electrode Potentials in Battery Electrolytes
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Abstract The electrode potential of Li metal is fundamental to the performance and stability of Li-metal batteries, yet its accurate prediction across diverse electrolyte chemistries remains a challenge. Standard quantum chemistry using cluster models fails to account for explicit bulk solvation, while ab initio molecular dynamics is restricted by the high computational cost of thermodynamic sampling. In this work, we present an integrated framework that combines a universal machine learning potential for electrolytes with a data-efficient fine-tuning strategy to compute Li electrode potentials. This workflow achieves ab initio level accuracy using ∼200 extra density functional theory calculations per electrolyte system. Furthermore, the identified relationship between local Li+ solvation environments and electrode potential shifts provides mechanistic insights into electrolyte-dependent redox behavior and offers guidance for rational electrolyte design.
papers.summary_ko: 범용 머신러닝 포텐셜과 데이터 효율적 미세조정 전략을 결합해 다양한 전해질 화학에서 리튬 금속의 전극 전위를 계산하는 통합 프레임워크를 제시했다. 전해질 시스템당 약 200회의 추가 DFT 계산만으로 ab initio 수준의 정확도를 달성하며, 국소 Li+ 솔베이션 환경과 전극 전위 변화 사이의 관계를 규명해 전해질 설계에 메커니즘적 지침을 제공한다.

papers.title: Coprecipitation‐Enabled Scalable Synthesis of High‐Energy Density Polyanion‐Integrated Disordered Rocksalt Cathodes for Lithium‐Ion Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Disordered rocksalt cathodes (DRX) represent a compelling platform for cobalt‐ and nickel‐free high‐energy density lithium‐ion batteries. Yet their scalable synthesis remains challenging, especially for metastable DRX chemistries that have been predominantly developed via mechanochemical routes. A prominent example is polyanion‐integrated DRX (DRXPS) cathodes, which rank among the best DRX cathodes reported to date in terms of reversible energy density, but have thus far been synthesized only mechanochemically via low‐temperature ball milling. Here we demonstrate a coprecipitation–enabled solid‐state synthesis of a DRXPS cathode, Li 1.67 Mn 1.5 P 0.17 O 4 , translating a mechanochemical route into a scalable process that is compatible with established cathode manufacturing infrastructure. The workflow programs precursor chemistry via coprecipitation of Mn 2 + with HPO 4 2 − and OH − , followed by a eutectic lithium‐salt‐assisted solid‐state reaction, enabling low‐thermal‐budget DRXPS formation (450°C, 30 min) in air. The reduced thermal budget suppresses particle coarsening and yields a mixed micro‐/nanoscale particle morphology, thereby eliminating the need for post‐synthesis particle pulverization. The resulting cathodes deliver 324 mAh g −1 (935 Wh kg −1 ), demonstrating that high‐energy density DRXPS can be realized within a manufacturing‐compatible workflow. This work establishes a direct pathway toward scalable production of metastable high‐energy density DRXPS cathodes and identifies precursor engineering as the key enabler.
papers.summary_ko: 공침-고상법을 결합하여 다각형 음이온이 통합된 무질서 암염형(DRX) 캐소드인 Li1.67Mn1.5P0.17O4를 스케일업 가능한 방식으로 합성했다. Mn2+와 HPO4²⁻, OH⁻의 공침으로 전구체 화학을 제어한 뒤 유테틱 리튬염 보조 저온(450°C, 30분) 고상 반응을 적용해 입자 조대화를 억제하고 별도의 분쇄 공정 없이 미크로/나노 혼합 입자 형태를 얻었다. 이 캐소드는 324 mAh/g(935 Wh/kg)의 고에너지밀도를 구현하여 기존 제조 인프라와 호환되는 DRX 양극 생산 경로를 제시했다.

papers.title: Towards the real diamond formation conditions: insights and perspective
papers.abstract_en: Pressure and temperature conditions of diamond formation provide valuable insights for reconstructing paleo-geotherms and the deep carbon cycle. These conditions can be determined by investigating mineral inclusions in diamonds using elastic geobarometry, which can be applied to any mineral inclusion in a diamond. However, it assumes purely elastic host-inclusion behaviour throughout exhumation. In reality, almost all mineral inclusions in diamonds are surrounded by cracks. Here, we combine in situ high-temperature micro-Raman spectroscopy with thermo-elastic modelling to evaluate the pressure-release process in one of the most common diamond inclusions, olivine [(Mg,Fe)2SiO4]. Our results indicate that a diamond can sustain pressures of ~2.5 GPa before undergoing minor fracturing, which induces only partial loss of inclusion pressure rather than a complete reset. The estimated pressure loss can lead to an underestimation of up to 2.5 GPa in the entrapment pressure at 1150 °C, a typical temperature for diamond formation. This study shows that olivine in diamond can undergo partial release of pressure during kimberlite eruptions due to fast adiabatic decompression, leading to cracked olivine inclusions and entrapment pressures underestimated by up to 2.5 GPa at 1150 °C
papers.summary_ko: 다이아몬드 내 감람석 포유물을 이용한 고온 라만분광과 열탄성 모델링으로 압력 해방 과정을 평가한 지구과학 연구다. 다이아몬드는 균열이 생기기 전까지 약 2.5 GPa의 압력을 견딜 수 있으며, 1150°C에서 포획 압력이 최대 2.5 GPa까지 과소평가될 수 있음을 밝혔다. 배터리 소재와는 관련이 없는 연구다.

papers.title: Thermodynamically Guided Antisite Ordering Stabilizes Cobalt‐Free Ultrahigh‐Ni Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Eliminating Co from ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes often exacerbates Li/Ni mixing, impeding Li + transport, amplifying reaction heterogeneity, and accelerating structural degradation. Most strategies focus on minimizing the overall degree of cation mixing, whereas thermodynamic control of antisite spatial organization remains underexplored. Here, we address this central stability challenge by developing a thermodynamics‐guided defect‐engineering strategy that stabilizes spatially correlated Li/Ni antisite configurations in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni cathodes. Density functional theory screening of high‐valence dopants reveals that Te 6+ exhibits the strongest energetic preference for spatially correlated antisite configurations. This prediction guides the synthesis of LiNi 0.948 Al 0.045 Te 0.007 O 2 containing coherent local antisite‐ordered superlattice domains. These ordered domains persist after prolonged cycling, strengthen interlayer coupling, suppress H2–H3 phase separation and c ‐axis contraction, and preserve low‐barrier Li + migration pathways. Local Te–O coordination further stabilizes lattice oxygen and mitigates oxygen‐loss‐induced surface reconstruction. Consequently, the cathode delivers 185 mAh g −1 at 10 C, retains 96.7% of its initial capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C with a 4.4 V cutoff, and retains 92% of its initial capacity after 100 cycles with a 4.6 V cutoff. These findings establish the spatial organization of defects as a critical design variable for mitigating the stability‐transport trade‐off in cobalt‐free ultrahigh‐Ni layered cathodes.
papers.summary_ko: 코발트를 포함하지 않는 초고니켈 층상 양극에서 Li/Ni 혼합이 심화되는 문제를 공간적으로 정렬된 안티사이트(antisite) 배열의 열역학적 제어로 해결한 연구이다. DFT 스크리닝을 통해 Te6+가 공간적으로 상관된 안티사이트 구조를 가장 선호함을 밝히고, 이를 바탕으로 LiNi0.948Al0.045Te0.007O2를 합성해 결맞음 안티사이트 정렬 초격자 도메인을 구현했다. 이 도메인은 장기 사이클 후에도 유지되어 층간 결합을 강화하고 H2-H3 상분리 및 c축 수축을 억제하며, 4.4V 컷오프 1C/200사이클에서 96.7%, 4.6V 컷오프 100사이클에서 92%의 용량 유지율을 보였다.

papers.abstract_en: High-temperature operation magnifies interfacial parasitic reactions in lithium metal batteries, rapidly depleting cyclable Li and destabilizing Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes. Here we introduce a reaction-priority gating strategy for ionic-liquid electrolytes...

papers.title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Electric power systems are evolving into cyber–physical infrastructures shaped by power electronics and digital control. As inverter-based generation alters system dynamics and digitalization heightens vulnerability to errors and attacks, cyber–physical coupling can also introduce subtle system-level effects. Here we show that grid-frequency time series worldwide exhibit a persistent 1-min oscillatory pattern whose origin has remained unexplained. We show that clock-synchronized control software in digitally controlled energy devices, particularly uninterruptible power supplies and battery energy storage systems, generates periodic power-demand peaks that propagate across voltage levels and can give rise to the observed pattern. The pattern amplitude has increased substantially in several grids over recent years, contributing to wear and tear in hydropower systems and motivating stricter frequency-control requirements. The rapid expansion of battery storage, data centres and the Internet-of-Things may further amplify such cyber–physical power oscillations, highlighting the need for improved control design.
papers.summary_ko: 전 세계 전력망 주파수에서 관찰되는 1분 주기 진동이 무정전전원장치(UPS)와 배터리 에너지저장시스템(BESS) 등 디지털 제어 기기의 시계 동기화에서 비롯됨을 규명한 연구다. 이 진동의 진폭이 여러 전력망에서 커지고 있어 수력발전 설비 마모와 주파수 제어 요건 강화 필요성을 지적한다. 배터리 소재 연구가 아닌 전력계통 분석 연구다.

papers.title: Machine Learning-Guided Precise Electrolyte Engineering Enables Stable Lithium Metal Pouch Cells Exceeding 350 Wh/kg at −40 °C
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Abstract High-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with wide-temperature adaptability are urgently needed for aerospace and military fields, yet extreme temperature conditions disrupt Li+ transport kinetics and cause failure in solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry regulation. To guide molecular selection for wide-temperature electrolyte design, we constructed Electrolyte-65K, a rule-defined library of electrolyte-relevant molecules, and trained D-P Compass using batch-computable molecular descriptors to efficiently predict and rank dipole moment (D) and polarizability (P). Applying the trained models to a literature-derived set of electrolyte molecule candidates, D-P Pareto analysis identified N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethanesulfonamide (DMTMSA) as the candidate at the Pareto knee. The thermally sensitive dipole–dipole interactions between DMTMSA and weakly solvating solvent 1,2-diethoxyethane (DEE) enable a temperature-autoresponsive electrolyte that maintains an anion-dominated solvation structure across a wide temperature range, enabling SEI chemistry engineering regulation from −40 to 60 °C. A 5.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 503.7 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C with a lifespan of 275 cycles and retains 365.5 Wh kg–1 at −40 °C with 99.8% capacity retention over 50 cycles. This work establishes a data-driven molecular screening framework for wide-temperature electrolyte engineering design.
papers.summary_ko: 머신러닝으로 쌍극자 모멘트와 분극률을 예측해 광범위한 온도에서 작동 가능한 리튬금속전지용 전해질을 설계한 연구다. 선별된 DMTMSA와 약솔베이팅 용매 DEE 조합은 온도에 따라 반응하는 음이온 지배형 솔베이션 구조를 형성해 SEI 화학을 −40~60°C 범위에서 조절한다. 5.8 Ah 파우치셀은 25°C에서 503.7 Wh/kg, −40°C에서도 365.5 Wh/kg의 에너지밀도와 높은 용량 유지율을 달성했다.

papers.title: Locally Competitive Coordination Electrolyte for High‐Voltage Lithium‐Metal Batteries With Ni‐Rich Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal anodes (LMAs) hold great promise to increase the energy density of batteries. This is especially true when using an energy‐dense cathode such as Ni‐rich layered transition metal oxides, but unfortunately, these lead to accelerated capacity loss when combined with LMAs. Ni‐rich cathodes suffer from surface reduction, which can be accelerated in contact with certain electrolyte solvents. This in turn leads to transition metal dissolution and shuttling, which poisons the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and complicates the anode stabilization. Here, we propose nitrile primary solvent combined with ether co‐solvent, diluent and two borate salts to suppress parasitic reaction. A competition in the ion coordination between solvents surrounded by diluents is achieved. This leads to the anions being preferentially decomposed in the SEI and enhanced reversibility. Using high cathode areal capacity (4.0 mAh cm − 2 ), thin LMAs (N/p = 2.5), lean electrolyte (3 g Ah − 1 ), and high charging voltages (≥4.4 V), we achieve a capacity retention of 80% over 250 cycles. With moderately high loading cathode (3.4 mAh cm − 2 ) but higher upper voltage (4.6 V), the cells retain 87.5% capacity retention over 430 cycles. Finally, we demonstrate Ah‐level anode‐free pouch cells with a 78.7% capacity retention over 100 cycles.
papers.summary_ko: 니켈리치 층상 양극과 리튬 금속음극(LMA)을 결합할 때 발생하는 표면 환원 및 전이금속 용해로 인한 SEI 오염 문제를 니트릴 주 용매와 에테르 공용매, 희석제, 두 종의 보레이트 염을 조합한 전해질로 해결했다. 용매 간 이온 배위 경쟁을 통해 음이온이 우선적으로 SEI에서 분해되도록 하여 가역성을 높였으며, 고면적용량 양극(4.0 mAh cm-2)과 얇은 리튬 음극, 린 전해질, 고전압(≥4.4V) 조건에서 250사이클 80% 용량 유지율을, 4.6V/3.4 mAh cm-2 조건에서는 430사이클 87.5% 유지율을 달성했다. 또한 Ah급 무음극 파우치셀에서도 100사이클 78.7% 용량 유지율을 입증했다.

papers.title: Fundamental Design Principles and Engineering Strategies of Liquid‐Phase Electrolytes for Highly Durable Rechargeable Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Lithium (Li) metal has emerged as the premier anode candidate in next-generation high-energy-density batteries due to its ultrahigh theoretical capacity and ultralow electrochemical potential. However, critical technical barriers persist in Li metal anode implementation, such as uncontrolled Li dendrite growth and persistent interfacial side reactions. Acting as the mediating agent between cathodes and anodes, electrolytes critically determine battery overall performance. Taking solvent-salt-additive components as the entry point, adopting liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies to optimize electrolyte composition and regulate solvation structure can not only address the inherent issues of Li metal anodes, but also endow Li metal batteries with desired performances, including high safety, high-voltage tolerance, fast-charging capability, and wide-temperature operation. In this review, the design principles of reliable liquid-phase electrolytes for Li metal batteries are discussed in detail. The essential liquid-phase electrolyte engineering strategies, including designing new-type salt/solvent molecular architectures, restructuring salt-solvent combination systems, incorporating electrolyte additives with various functions, utilizing (localized) high-concentration electrolytes, and developing brand-new electrolyte formulations for adapting to different temperature ranges, are comprehensively summarized. Moreover, emerging design strategies, future design considerations, and remaining challenges in electrolyte engineering are highlighted, with the aim of pointing out potential opportunities to propel the practical development of Li metal batteries.
papers.summary_ko: 리튬금속전지용 액상 전해질의 설계 원리와 공학적 전략을 종합한 리뷰 논문이다. 염/용매 분자 구조 설계, 염-용매 조합 재구성, 첨가제 도입, (국소) 고농도 전해질, 온도 적응형 전해질 개발 등을 통해 리튬 덴드라이트 성장과 계면 부반응 문제를 해결하는 방안을 다룬다. 고전압 내성, 고속충전, 광온도 작동 실현을 위한 향후 과제도 제시한다.

papers.title: Engineering Li + Transport in Ni‐Rich Layered Cathodes Toward Homogenization
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Nickel‐rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg −1 , but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li + transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li + transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo‐mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li + transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport‐centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross‐scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport‐centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next‐generation high‐energy‐density cathode materials.
papers.summary_ko: 니켈리치 층상산화물(NRLO, Ni≥80%) 양극의 원자, 구조, 계면 수준에서 발생하는 불균일한 Li+ 수송이 상변화, 미세균열, 표면 재구성 등 거시적 화학-기계적 퇴화로 이어지는 과정을 다룬 리뷰이다. 수송 균질화(transport homogenization)를 통합 설계 원칙으로 제시하며 벌크 구조 설계, 계면 수송 엔지니어링, 동적 수송 조절 등 다양한 전략을 수송 중심 관점에서 재해석하고, 수송 이질성을 정량화하는 특성분석 기법과 향후 예측적 설계 원칙 수립 방향을 논의한다.

papers.title: Electric‐Field‐Coupled Heterointerface Engineering via Li/F Co‐Doping for Enhanced Rate Capability and Interfacial Stability of Fe/Mn‐Based Layered Sodium Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT P2‐type Fe/Mn‐based layered oxide materials have long been plagued by structural degradation, air sensitivity, and interfacial instability, which severely restrict their application in sodium‐ion batteries. Herein, we propose an in situ modification strategy integrating bulk Li/F co‐doping with a surface heterojunction coating and successfully synthesize Na 0.67 Fe 0.35 Mn 0.5 Li 0.15 O 1.93 F 0.07 (LMO@NFMLOF). IDPC‐STEM reveals the heterogeneous structure comprising distinct inner and outer regions. DFT calculations confirm the presence of a built‐in electric field at the heterointerface. The experimental results demonstrate that bulk Li/F co‐doping enhances crystal stability, while the built‐in electric field generated by the surface heterojunction accelerates Na + kinetic processes, and the coating further improves air and interfacial stability. Consequently, the LMO@NFMLOF cathode delivers a discharge capacity of 110 mAh g − 1 after 200 cycles at 2C. Remarkably, it maintains a discharge capacity of 85.6 mAh g − 1 after 300 cycles at 5C, demonstrating outstanding rate capability and cycling stability. This synergistic bulk‐surface optimization provides a new approach for designing high‐rate layered oxide cathodes.
papers.summary_ko: P2형 Fe/Mn 기반 층상 소듐 양극재의 구조 열화와 계면 불안정성을 해결하기 위해 벌크 Li/F 공도핑과 표면 헤테로접합 코팅을 결합한 Na0.67Fe0.35Mn0.5Li0.15O1.93F0.07(LMO@NFMLOF)를 합성했다. DFT 계산으로 헤테로계면에 내부전기장이 형성되어 Na+ 이동을 가속함을 확인했으며, 코팅은 대기 및 계면 안정성을 향상시킨다. 이 양극재는 2C에서 200사이클 후 110 mAh/g, 5C에서 300사이클 후 85.6 mAh/g의 방전용량을 유지했다.

papers.summary_ko: 유전체 특성을 설계한 분리막을 통해 상용 리튬이온전지의 초고속 충전을 가능하게 하는 연구로 추정된다. (제목 기반 추정)

papers.title: Constructing an Adaptive Flexible Interphase on Halide Electrolytes by Lewis‐Acid‐Induced Polymerization for High‐Voltage All‐Solid‐State Lithium Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) combining halide solid electrolytes (HSEs) with high‐nickel layered oxide cathodes offer great promise for high energy density, yet they suffer from severe interfacial issues such as oxidative decomposition, mechanical degradation, and chemical incompatibility with sulfide electrolytes. Herein, we report a Lewis‐acid‐induced surface‐softening strategy that constructs a nanoscale adaptive flexible interphase (AFI) via in situ polymerization of acrylonitrile (AN) on a representative halide electrolyte, Li 3 InCl 6 (LIC). The resulting AFI layer concurrently provides ionic conductivity, excellent oxidation stability (>4.8 V), and favorable viscoelasticity, thereby synergistically enhancing the electrochemical, chemical, and mechanical stability of the interface without compromising bulk ion transport. When paired with a single‐crystal ultrahigh‑nickel cathode LiNi 0.94 Co 0.05 Mn 0.01 O 2 (Ni94), the surface‑softened LIC (S‑LIC) enables ASSLBs delivering specific capacities of 223.8 and 209.5 mAh g −1 at 2 C and 4 C, respectively, retaining over 85% of the initial capacity after 2000 cycles at 2 C, and operate stably for more than 9000 cycles at 10 C. Even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.8 V, a capacity retention of 81% is achieved after 800 cycles at 2 C. This work provides a broadly applicable and efficient interfacial engineering route for high‑voltage halide‑based ASSLBs.

papers.title: Constructing Hybrid Solid–Liquid Li+ Transport Networks for Fast-Charging Thick Electrodes
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Fast-charging technology for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries remains constrained by high interfacial impedance and sluggish Li+ transport within electrodes. Herein, hierarchical-sized Li1.5Al0.5Ti1.5(PO4)3 (LATP, particle ranging from 5 to 500 nm) is used to construct a hybrid solid–liquid Li+ transport network in high-mass-loading cathodes (27 mg cm–2). A combination of different characterization techniques is employed to understand the underlying working principle of LATP from the particle to the electrode scale. LATP nanograins (∼10 nm) adsorbed onto cathode particle surfaces reduce Li+ desolvation energy (43.30 vs 52.97 kJ mol–1) and stabilize a thin CEI after cycling. Submicron LATP particles (320–480 nm) infiltrate pores of thick electrodes, forming interconnected networks that increase the Li+ diffusion coefficient. Furthermore, LATP increases the Li+ transference number of the liquid electrolyte within LATP-permeated regions. Consequently, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li cells with LATP-blended cathodes deliver dramatically enhanced rate performance (102 vs 36 mAh g–1 at 0.75C and –10 °C).

papers.title: Toward Practical Zn‐Ion Batteries Through Separator/Electrolyte Co‐Design
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT While substantial research effort has been paid to address short‐circuits and parasitic hydrogen evolution reactions (HER) in Zn‐ion batteries (ZIBs), a remaining challenge that is often overlooked is ZIB separators. Currently, thick glass fiber (GF) separators are used, which unnecessarily reduce the volumetric cell performance and lead to non‐uniform Zn plating/stripping. Unfortunately, separators optimized for Li‐ion batteries are intrinsically hydrophobic and therefore incompatible with aqueous ZIB systems. Here, we propose using a hybrid organic‐aqueous electrolyte which is compatible with thin polypropylene (PP) separators developed for Li‐ion batteries. The hybrid electrolyte, together with the PP separator, enables uniform Zn plating and suppresses HER. Combined, these effects allow for stable cycling for 4360 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 3 mAh cm −2 in a Zn symmetrical cell. Further, replacing the currently used 350 µm‐thick GF separator with our proposed 23 µm PP separator can increase the energy densities of multi‐layer pouch cells by over 2.5‐fold. Finally, Zn//NVO full cells using our hybrid electrolyte and separator demonstrate stable cycling performance for over 200 cycles at a high areal capacity of 4.4 mAh cm −2 , demonstrating that electrolyte/separator co‐design is an overlooked strategy toward practical ZIBs.

papers.title: Ion‐Electron Convergent Interphases Enable Ultrahigh Sulfur Utilization for All‐Solid‐State Li–S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state batteries offer a safer route toward electrochemical energy storage with high energy density, but the active‐material utilization is commonly limited by unbalanced carrier transport dynamics through spatially decoupled delivery pathways, which overlap only at restricted reaction fronts. Such an issue is particularly severe for electronically and ionically insulating sulfur/Li 2 S, making efficient sulfur conversion the key bottleneck for practical all‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs). Here, we propose surface‐bound ion‐electron convergent interphases on the Li 2 S surface that reconstruct localized triple‐phase contacts into an integrated active surface. Using the effective magnetic moment, originating from spin asymmetry, as a screening criterion for interfacial affinity, Li 2 FeS 2 is identified to form a robust surface‐bound interphase with Li 2 S, which bridges separated ion and electron pathways at the reaction areas, decreasing the transport tortuosity and lowering the activation barriers for both Li 2 S oxidation and reduction. Consequently, ASSLSBs stably work over 10 000 cycles at 1 mg cm −2 while delivering a loading‐insensitive sulfur utilization of 97.8% and 95.8% at 1 and 8 mg cm −2 , respectively. Moreover, a record areal capacity of 38.69 mAh cm −2 is achieved, highlighting the spatially surface‐bound mixed conductors as an effective design principle for synchronizing coupled ion‐electron transfer (CIET) in all‐solid‐state batteries.

papers.title: From Localized Electrochemical Behavior to Interfacial Reaction Mechanisms: Evaluation of Corrosion Inhibitors for Active Pb-Containing Phases in Sanxingdui Embrittled Gold Masks
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Abstract The Sanxingdui gold masks are Au–Ag–Pb ternary alloys in which preferential corrosion of intergranular active Pb-containing phases causes severe embrittlement and threatens long-term preservation. Here, corrosion inhibitors for these vulnerable microdomains were evaluated by integrating microstructural characterization, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Sodium cysteinate (NaCys), sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP), sodium silicate (NaSi), and sodium salts of saturated fatty acids (NaCn, C6–C18) were screened on simulated Au–Ag–Pb alloys. NaCys and SHMP induced pronounced Pb depletion, while NaSi formed a hydrophilic, cracked deposit with limited protection. In contrast, NaCn showed a pronounced but non-monotonic carbon-chain-length dependence. NaC9, NaC10, and NaC12 exhibited the best overall performance, with NaC10 providing the highest and most stable localized inhibition. Shorter chains produced less ordered and less hydrophobic films, whereas longer chains were limited by poor effective solubility and interfacial accessibility. DFT calculations showed that inhibition cannot be predicted from adsorption strength alone. By combining adsorption energy, Pb defect formation energy, and interfacial retention energy, we established an interfacial reaction criterion distinguishing stable film formation from inhibitor-induced Pb extraction, thereby introducing the concept of effective inhibitor interfacial reactivity for mechanism-guided conservation. This approach provides a targeted strategy for protecting Sanxingdui gold masks and other complex multiphase metallic heritage objects.

papers.title: Entropy Stabilized Li‐Rich Layered Oxide Nanoparticles for Advanced High‐Voltage Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The performance enhancement of emerging flexible batteries relies on the development of advanced small‐particle electrode materials. However, current cathode materials with reduced particle size mostly suffer from low operating voltage, especially aqueous based electrodes. In this study, by using laser‐induced carbothermal method, we successfully fabricated high‐entropy doped Li‐rich nanoparticles as layered oxide cathodes that exhibit outstanding high‐voltage performances. The direct bottom–up nanocrystal growth enables the formation of such exclusive Li‐rich nanoparticles with unprecedentedly small diameter of 83.08 nm. As confirmed by atomic‐resolution imaging, operando x‐ray diffraction and synchrotron techniques analysis, the cathode achieves high lattice stability at elevated cut‐off voltage through the combined effects of heteroatomic composition and reduced particle diameters. Molecular dynamics simulations using machine‐learning interatomic potentials further demonstrate suppressed oxygen loss and stabilized transition‐metal framework in the high‐entropy doped cathodes. Consequently, the cathode operates steadily at voltage window of 2.5–4.8 V with ultrahigh power density of 877.9 Wh kg −1 at 1 C. The assembled full cell and fiber battery provide significant practical feasibility during high‐voltage cycling. This work provides an efficient strategy for designing high‐voltage flexible batteries, offering critical insights for next‐generation energy storage research.

papers.title: Closed‐Pore Engineering Couples Sodium Confinement and Interfacial Stabilization for Dendrite‐Resistant Hard Carbon Anodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Hard carbon, a leading anode for sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), suffers from nonuniform sodium deposition, which causes dendrite growth and compromises safety and cycle life. Here, we report a closed‐pore engineering strategy based on cobalt‐doped hard carbon (CoHC) that couples internal sodium‐cluster confinement with interfacial stabilization. Internally, the closed nanopores redirect sodium storage from surface accumulation to deep pore filling, thereby inhibiting the growth of quasi‐metallic sodium clusters and dendrite propagation. Externally, the closed‐pore architecture regulates interfacial chemistry, leading to a thin, uniform, inorganic‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) with reduced charge‐transfer resistance. In situ electrochemical tests confirm stable interfaces and suppressed dendrite growth in both Na||CoHC half cells and CoHC||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP) full cells, whereas severe dendritic deposition occurs on pristine hard carbon (HC) under identical current density. The CoHC anode delivers superior cycling stability with a capacity retention of 95% after 500 cycles, significantly outperforming HC. This work paves the way for dendrite‐resistant, safer, and longer‐lasting sodium‐ion batteries.

papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Gel zinc‐air batteries (GZABs) are promising for flexible energy storage. However, their performance is often limited by unstable gel cathode interfaces, where water‐dependent OH − transport, charge transfer, and mechanical adhesion are closely linked. Here, we propose an interfacial coupling chemistry by using a cobalt‐based Prussian blue analogue (CCN) as a reconstructable precatalyst. When assembled with a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) gel electrolyte and electrochemically activated during the GZAB operation, CCN was reconstructed into a sheet‐arrayed amorphous CoOOH while releasing cyanide‐derived nitrogen that was confined by the gel network and converted into −NO 2 groups at the PVA/CoOOH interface. These NO 2 groups act as molecular linkers, chemically coupling with CoOOH through Co–N–O bonding and reinforcing hydrogen bonding with the PVA chains. The in situ reconstructed electrode exhibits enhanced interfacial OH − transport, with an apparent diffusion coefficient 3.25 times that of the ex situ construction, together with lower interfacial resistance and stronger mechanical adhesion. Benefiting from both the reconstructed CoOOH catalyst and coupling interface, the resulting GZAB delivers a peak power density of 144 mW cm −2 and maintains 86.4 mW cm −2 even at 30% water content. The enhanced interfacial adhesion further enables stable operation in omnidirectionally flexible cable‐type zinc‐air batteries.

papers.title: Sulfur-Induced Local Structure Reconstruction and Weak Na–Anion Interactions Enable Fast Na+ Transport in x Na2S-TaCl5 Electrolytes
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Amorphous solid electrolytes offer opportunities for fast ion transport, yet the structural origins governing their performance remain difficult to resolve due to the absence of long-range order. While mixed-anion strategies have recently emerged to improve ion transport in sodium halide electrolytes, how sulfur incorporation modifies the local structure and Na+ transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a series of xNa2S-TaCl5 mixed anion solid electrolytes to elucidate the impact of sulfur on the structure and Na+ transport. Structural analyses reveal that sulfur incorporation reconstructs the connectivity of Ta-centered polyhedra while progressively disrupting the long-range crystalline ordering to form an amorphous framework. More importantly, neutron pair distribution function analysis reveals the sulfur-induced reconstruction of the local Ta-centered structure, with the emergence of coexisting edge-sharing- and corner-sharing-like motifs from the isolated polyhedra in crystalline NaTaCl6. Simulations further show that sulfur shifts the local polyhedral connectivity toward a larger proportion of edge-sharing configurations relative to the O-containing analogue. Matched-composition machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) comparing O- and S-containing amorphous models suggest that sulfur weakens Na-anion binding, shortens Na–anion residence times, and lowers the barrier for Na+ migration relative to the O analogue. As a result, the optimized composition achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 3.25 mS cm–1 with a low activation energy of 0.28 eV. When evaluated in all-solid-state sodium batteries with an uncoated NaNi1/3Mn1/3Fe1/3O2 cathode, the cell delivers a discharge capacity of 112 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles (82.6% retention) with a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%, demonstrating stable interfacial compatibility with uncoated layered oxide cathodes.

papers.title: Photothermal Catalytic Dry Reforming of Methane With 1000‐Hour Stability via Redox Shuttle of Metal Vanadate
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Photothermal catalytic dry reforming of methane (DRM) mediated by lattice oxygen (O l ) is promising for converting two major greenhouse gases into syngas. However, conventional oxide supports possess strong metal–oxygen bonds that restrict O l migration, compromising stability, typically less than 200 h. Herein, we design a Rh/Mg 2 V 1.33 O 4 catalyst with Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + interfacial sites ( n = 3 or 4). The defective spinel vanadate support exhibits quasi‐metallic properties, enabling efficient solar harvesting and photothermal conversion. Under 4 W cm −2 light irradiation without external heating, the redox flexibility of V species enables an interfacial redox shuttle (Rh δ + ─O v ─V n + ⇌ Rh δ + ─O l ─V ( n +1)+ ), which endows the catalyst with effective O l migration and regeneration ability in the DRM reaction. This property steers the reaction along a coking‐resistant CH 3 O* pathway and guarantees structural stability. As a result, the catalyst delivers long‐term stability for 1000 h, outperforming state‐of‐the‐art photothermal catalysts. It also achieves high syngas generation rates of 16.1 and 18.6 mol g Rh −1 h −1 for H 2 and CO, respectively, along with a light‐to‐chemical energy efficiency of ∼20.9%. This work establishes quasi‐metallic, redox‐active vanadate supports as a transformative platform for durable O l ‐mediated photothermal catalysis.

papers.title: Non‐Monotonical Ion Association Equilibria in Low‐Temperature Sodium–Metal Battery Electrolytes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low‐temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity‐based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self‐association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non‐monotonical temperature‐dependent Na + solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature. In line with this consideration, a facile strategy using a dilute electrolyte was developed to establish a favorable solvation equilibrium between dissociated and associated species. This work refreshes the understanding of thermodynamic equilibrium between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions, and challenges the conventional approach of learning from the lithium batteries that encourage weakly solvating electrolyte, arguing the critical importance of strengthening cation solvation chemistry in Na battery field due to the temperature‐dependent dipole–dipole interactions.

papers.title: Facile Polyiodides Conversion Enabled by Facet Engineering for Durable Zinc–Iodine Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are highly promising for grid-scale energy storage, yet their practical viability is severely plagued by the polyiodides shuttle effect and sluggish liquid–solid conversion kinetics, which fundamentally arise from the contradictory energetic demands between soluble intermediate confinement and solid-product desorption. Herein, we rationally construct a dual-facet spinel cobalt oxide to precisely decouple these competing interfacial behaviors. By regulating the proportional exposure of strongly coordinating (100) and weakly coordinating (111) facets, a tailored surface microenvironment is constructed that effectively circumvents the inherent thermodynamic trade-off, breaking the single adsorption limitation intrinsic to uniform catalysts. In situ iodine L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and three-dimensional synchrotron-based nanocomputed tomography reveal that this specific facet modulation substantially reduces the activation barrier for rate-determining polyiodides oxidation, facilitating spatially uniform solid-iodine deposition. Driven by these structural advantages, the assembled Zn–I2 batteries with c/o-Co3O4 deliver a high specific capacity of 161.1 mAh g–1 at 16 A g–1 and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.00055% per cycle after 50,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Furthermore, the batteries also exhibit a broad operational temperature ranging from −30 to 60 °C, highlighting the strong potential for practical applications. This work provides a perspective on facet engineering for achieving wide-temperature-tolerant aqueous iodine storage.

papers.title: Operando X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Reveals Oxide Solid Electrolyte Stability against Electrochemically Plated Lithium
papers.abstract_en: Abstract X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

papers.title: Interfacial and Hydration‐Associated Lithium Retention During FePO 4 Regeneration from Spent LiFePO 4 Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Selective FePO 4 precipitation is used to separate iron and phosphorus from lithium during hydrometallurgical recycling of spent LiFePO 4 , yet measurable lithium can remain in the regenerated FePO 4 precursor. Here, lithium partitioning was examined in a simulated Fe–P system, a commercial LiFePO 4 ‐derived leachate, and a spent black‐mass‐derived leachate. Sequential washing resolved the lithium associated with the precipitates into fractions with different accessibility. Under representative conditions, approximately 70% of the retained lithium was washing‐removable, whereas approximately 30% remained after three washing cycles. Contact with lithium‐free FePO 4 resulted in an apparent 2.13% decrease in dissolved Li concentration, approaching a plateau within 10 min. Thermodynamic analysis indicated that the formation of the considered discrete lithium‐containing precipitates was unfavorable, while changes in hydration and local Fe–O–P environments correlated with the washing‐retained fraction. These results support a proposed precipitation‐associated model involving lithium retention in environments with different accessibility within hydrated amorphous FePO 4 . The findings identify precipitation and washing as linked control stages for managing lithium carryover during FePO 4 regeneration.

Cascade Catalysis of Zn/Nb Single‐Atom Sites for Wide‐Temperature Li‐S Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium‐sulfur batteries are considered promising next‐generation energy‐storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density. However, their practical applications are severely hindered by sluggish sulfur redox kinetics and lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) shuttling, which are significantly aggravated under extreme‐temperature conditions. To address this issue, a novel cascade catalysis strategy is developed to regulate the multistep sulfur redox process through embedding the Nb‐N 4 and Zn‐N 4 dual single‐atom sites within N, P co‐doped carbon fibers (Zn/Nb‐NPMCFs). In conjunction with theoretical analysis, it is clarified that Nb single‐atom site preferentially adsorbs soluble LiPSs through forming an Nb‐S bond and catalyzes their conversion, whereas Zn single‐atom site facilitates subsequent Li 2 S‐related redox conversion. With the cascade catalysis effect enabling accelerated sulfur conversion and suppressed LiPSs shuttling, the assembled Li‐S batteries with Zn/Nb‐NPMCFs as free‐standing sulfur hosts deliver good electrochemical performance over a wide temperature range, retaining 651.8 and 401.1 mAh g −1 under 50°C and −20°C at 0.5 C, even after 500 cycles, respectively. This work provides a guideline for improving multistep sulfur redox kinetics in Li‐S batteries.

papers.title: Thermally Robust Piezoelectric KNN/Polyimide Separator for Regulating Lithium Deposition in Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium‐metal batteries offer exceptionally high theoretical energy density but are hindered by dendrite‐induced short circuits and the limited thermal stability of conventional separators. Here, we report a thermally robust piezoelectric composite separator composed of highly fluorinated polyimide and potassium sodium niobate (KNN), fabricated through an electrospinning/imidization strategy. Molecular dipole engineering, preferential through‐thickness polarization, and ceramic‐polymer electromechanical coupling collectively enable regulation of the local interfacial electric field, homogenized Li + flux, and suppressed lithium dendrite growth during cycling. Meanwhile, the rigid polyimide framework endows the separator with excellent thermal tolerance and structural integrity at elevated temperatures. Consequently, LiFePO 4 ||Li cells retain 88.5% of their initial capacity after 1900 cycles at 2 C. This work demonstrates an electromechanically active separator that integrates intrinsic thermal stability with interfacial regulation, providing a potential strategy for improving the durability of lithium‐metal batteries.
