papers.title: Mechanochemically Disordered Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 Oxyhalide Unlocks Superionic Conductivity (>10 mS.cm −1 )
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT All‐solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries (ASSBs) offer a promising route to surpass the energy‐density limits of conventional lithium‐ion technology. However, their commercialization is hindered by interfacial instability, chemo‐mechanical degradation, and the limited ionic conductivity of current solid electrolytes, driving the search for new fast‐ion conductors, particularly among lithium oxyhalides. Here, we report a new lithium tantalum oxychloride, Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 , synthesized via a simple low‐temperature route. The material crystallizes in a triclinic structure composed of isolated [Ta 2 OCl 10 ] 2− dimers and exhibits a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 0.002 mS.cm − 1 . Ball milling dramatically enhances Li + transport, increasing the conductivity by a factor of 5000 to 11 mS.cm −1 while reducing the activation energy from 0.46 to 0.27 eV. Combined structural, spectroscopic, and computational analyses reveal that this enhancement originates from the formation of a highly disordered, liquid‐like Li + sublattice. Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 further demonstrates a stability window of 1.89–3.70 V vs. Li x In and enables ASSBs with low polarization and excellent capacity retention (700 cycles at 1C with decay less than 20%). These results establish Li 2 Ta 2 OCl 10 as a promising superionic conductor and highlight the Li–M–O–Cl family as a fertile design space for next‐generation solid electrolytes.

papers.title: Making 1000 Wh/kg LiNiO2 Cathode Nearly Strain-Free by Complex-Concentrated Doping
papers.abstract_en: Abstract High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.

papers.title: Helical Keratin‐Derived Aqueous Binders for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur batteries (LSBs) possess ultrahigh energy density, low cost, and environmental friendliness, making them strong contenders for next‐generation energy storage technologies. However, their development is hindered by multiple interfacial challenges, including the shuttling of lithium polysulfides (LiPS), sluggish reaction kinetics, and severe volume expansion of the cathode. To address these issues, a multifunctional biomass‐derived aqueous binder was designed by crosslinking an α‐helical protein (α‐HP) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and glycerol (GL). The α ‐helical structure of α‐HP in the α‐HP/PVA/GL adhesive acts as a “molecular spring”, effectively buffering volume expansion and stabilizing the electrode structure. Additionally, its abundant N‐ and O‐containing polar groups efficiently anchor LiPS, significantly suppressing the shuttling effect and accelerating redox kinetics. Consequently, lithium‐sulfur batteries employing the α‐HP/PVA/GL binder exhibit exceptional long‐term cycling stability. The α‐HP/PVA/GL cathode delivers an initial discharge specific capacity of 737.3 mAh g −1 and retains 487.9 mAh g −1 after 600 stable cycles at 2 C, with an average capacity decay rate of only 0.056% per cycle. This study provides a green, facile, and efficient strategy for developing multifunctional binders to overcome practical bottlenecks in lithium‐sulfur battery applications.

papers.title: A bulk-surface co-modification strategy enabling stable operation of ultrahigh-nickel Li(Ni0.96Co0.03Mn0.01)O2 cathode beyond 4.7 V
papers.abstract_en: Ultrahigh-nickel layered Li(Ni x Co y Mn z )O 2 ( x ≥0.9) holds substantial promise for use as cathode-active materials to boost the energy density of lithium-ion batteries. However, they typically suffer rapid performance degradation under high-voltage operation. Herein, we report the synthesis of Li(Ni 0.96 Co 0.03 Mn 0.01 )O 2 (NCM96) and design an integrated bulk-surface co-modification strategy that combines low-dose Zr bulk incorporation (2000 ppm relative to the total transition-metal content) with sequential surface modifications by Al 2 O 3 /TiO 2 and H 3 BO 3 (M-NCM96). The M-NCM96 cathode is assessed under various voltage windows in lithium metal cells, which delivers a specific capacity as high as 252.2 mAh g –1 when operated at a high cutoff voltage of 5.0 V and maintain reasonably good capacity retention of 74.2% after 100 cycles. Moreover, in the optimized voltage window of 2.6 – 4.7 V at 25°C, the M-NCM96 cathode affords an initial capacity of 196.1 mAh g –1 at 1.0 C and exhibits 91.3% capacity retention after 200 cycles. Furthermore, M-NCM96 also demonstrates good performance in pouch cells, confirming that the co-modification strategy is effective at the device level. Comprehensive characterization and density functional theory calculations indicate that Zr-mediated bulk stabilization and Al/Ti/B-derived surface protection cooperatively mitigate lattice breathing, microcrack initiation/propagation, gas evolution, and electrode-electrolyte interfacial degradation, thereby enabling markedly improved cycling stability under high-voltage operation.

papers.title: Suppressing Irreversible Interfacial Spatial Electron Transfer for High‐Temperature 4.6 V LiCoO 2
papers.abstract_en: (LCO) cathodes under elevated temperatures is essential for meeting the growing energy-storage demands across diverse applications. However, it is severely hindered by interfacial parasitic reactions arising from irreversible electron transfer between electrolyte solvents and the cathode. Herein, we demonstrate the regulation of the spatial distance and orientation of phosphate solvent molecules within the electric double layer at the LCO interface, thereby fundamentally suppressing irreversible interfacial spatial electron transfer (ISET) under combined high-voltage and high-temperature conditions. The fluorinated bidentate phosphate ester (TEFP) creates a compact solvation sheath that counteracts the interfacial-electric-field-driven enrichment of phosphate solvents, increases the solvent-cathode distance, and maintains a P═O orientation away from the cathode, thereby suppressing ISET from the P═O bond to the delithiated LCO. This simultaneously promotes the formation of a well-controlled, uniform, and stable cathode-electrolyte interphase. Consequently, Li||LCO cells with TEFP electrolyte deliver superior cycling stability at 4.6 V and elevated temperatures, with 80% capacity retention after 760 cycles at 60°C and 75.5% after 300 cycles at 80°C, while Ah-level pouch cells further validate the practical viability of the electrolyte. This work provides guidance for the design of cathode interfaces under high-voltage and high-temperature conditions.

papers.title: Spatial Redistribution of Intrinsic Cation Disorder Toward Ultra‐Stable Regeneration of LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 Cathode
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Conventional direct regeneration of spent LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 cathode material typically aims to eliminate structural defects, such as disordered cation mixing in the bulk phase and electrochemically inert rock‐salt phase formed on the surface. Such regeneration processes feature simple procedures, enabling efficient reconstruction of crystal ordering and effective capacity restoration. However, perfectly ordered layered structures are inherently unstable during long‐term charge–discharge cycling. Here, we propose a defect‐empowered regeneration strategy that rationally modulates and harnesses Li/Ni cation disorder instead of completely eradicating such defects. The electrochemically inert rock–salt phase was dismantled, while intermittent nickel was intentionally retained within lithium slabs. Regeneration was completed within 30 min, outpacing conventional approaches by orders of magnitude. The regenerated material delivered an initial discharge capacity of 164.39 mAh g −1 at 0.2C. It exhibited near 100% capacity retention after 100 cycles at 0.5C and 200 cycles at 1C, demonstrating significantly enhanced stability. Our findings reframe cation disorder as an effective lattice stabilizer, offering a rapid and sustainable pathway for battery recycling.

papers.title: Reusable and Robust Hydrogel With Dynamic Sacrificial S─S Bonds: In Situ Construction of an Integrated SEI/Hydrogel Interface for Highly Stable Zn–I 2 Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The trade‐off among mechanical strength, ionic conductivity, and interfacial stability remains a core challenge for high‐performance hydrogel interfacial layers. Herein, an integrated SEI/polyurea–polyurethane hydrogel (PUMA) interface was constructed on the Zn anode via in situ gelation coupled with interfacial electrochemical reduction. Polyurea–polyurethane hard segments containing octuple H‐bonds, Zn 2+ coordination bonds, and dynamic S─S bonds reinforce PUMA through multi‐level energy dissipation and suppress side reactions by regulating interfacial water. Polyanionic soft segments rich in carboxyl and sulfonic acid groups construct low‐barrier, ion‐selective pathways, optimizing Zn 2+ transport and deposition by solvation regulation and mitigation of concentration polarization. Crucially, interfacial sacrificial S─S bonds undergo cleavage during electrochemical reduction, generating an integrated SEI/PUMA interface with enhanced interfacial stability. The dynamic polyanionic network also blocks polyiodide shuttling and enables thermal reprocessing. Consequently, PUMA@Zn achieves a Zn 2+ transference number of 0.79 and symmetric cell cycling for 5080 h (1 mA cm −2 and 0.5 mAh cm −2 ). PUMA@Zn//I 2 cells retain 88% capacity after 43 000 cycles at 4 A g −1 and operate for over 11 000 cycles even at high iodine loading (16.58 mg cm −2 ). This strategy provides a novel pathway to achieve robust, ion‐conductivity, and chemically bonded hydrogel–metal interfaces for high‐performance aqueous batteries.

papers.title: Mechanistic Insights of Jahn–Teller Effect Suppression in High-Entropy Prussian Blue Analogue Cathodes
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: The Jahn-Teller (J-T) effect, as discovered by Hermann Jahn and Edward Teller in 1937, often causes lattice distortion and structural instability in Mn-based battery materials. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy design may help suppress J-T distortion, yet the underlying mechanism remains largely elusive due to their compositional complexity and structural disorder. Herein, using a Mn-based Prussian blue analogue as a case study, we employed a machine learning interatomic potential combined with synchrotron extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) to elucidate the fundamental mechanism of the J-T suppression in high-entropy materials. Unexpectedly, EXAFS spectra reveal the absence of the typical J-T Mn-N bond-length splitting in our high-entropy Prussian blue analogue sample, but instead a broader Mn-N bond-length distribution. Machine learning-assisted calculations demonstrate the [MnN6] octahedra exhibit randomly oriented distortions along x-, y-, and z-axes in high-entropy lattices, resulting in the local distortion averaging out at the macroscopic scale. Further analysis of the local Mn coordination environment reveals that the high-entropy configuration enhances d-electron delocalization and reduces the energy splitting between Mn dx2-y2 and dz2 orbitals. This allows two structurally and electronically distinct distortion modes to coexist within the lattice, which disrupts long-range cooperative J-T order. Strikingly, the ultralong cycling stability of high-entropy K0.46[Mn0.21Co0.19Ni0.21Cu0.20Zn0.19][Fe(CN)6]0.98·1.69H2O is experimentally demonstrated, achieving 91.0% capacity retention over 50,000 cycles for aqueous ammonium-ion storage, which surpasses all of the Mn-based rechargeable batteries to date. Our study uncovers the microscopic mechanism of J-T suppression in high-entropy materials and provides an effective strategy for designing durable high-entropy battery electrodes.

papers.title: High-Performance LiNiO2 Cathodes through Microstructural Engineering
papers.abstract_en: Abstract LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.

papers.title: From Coacervates to Ordered Lattices: Sequence‐Guided Condensation of Polyelectrolyte Complexes Through Designed Coiled‐Coil Peptides
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Electrostatic complexation of oppositely charged biomacromolecules produces a spectrum of condensed phases, from liquid coacervates to ordered solids. Yet the underlying amino acid sequence‐level rules remain poorly understood. Here, we utilize computationally designed coiled‐coil peptide “bundlemers” as a programmable platform to systematically investigate these principles. This study demonstrates that precise control over the material phase formed through electrostatic complexation is achieved through subtle amino acid sequence modifications. By tuning coiled coil terminal motifs and surface charge distribution, bundlemer‐polypeptide complexation can span liquid coacervates, soft solids, or solid precipitates. Specifically, bundlemer coiled coil nanoparticles with +24 charge were complexed with different lengths of polyanionic polypeptide. Nanoparticles with a mixed charge character containing both acidic and basic amino acids produced coacervate phases. When the bundlemers displayed only basic amino acids making a single charge‐type +24 nanoparticle, solid precipitates with specific hexagonal lattice symmetry were formed. When the charge character was flipped with negatively charged bundlemers and positively charged polypeptide, similar hexagonally packed complexes were formed. This work establishes a robust framework for programming the self‐assembly of polyelectrolyte‐based soft matter, offering a sequence‐guided pathway from disordered liquid condensates to precisely defined, ordered nanomaterials.

papers.title: Asymmetric coordination engineering of single-atom catalysts for high-performance lithium–sulfur batteries under practical conditions
Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Anion‐dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low‐temperature sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature‐sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion‐cation‐targeted regulation via Sn(OTf) 2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent‐reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na 15 Sn 4 ), which goes beyond the prevailing anion‐centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn 2+ ‐Na + coordination excludes PF 6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf − and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent‐dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na + desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah‐scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg −1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade‐off between low‐temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

papers.title: Moderate Li–N Coordination Between Dibromopyrazine and Polysulfides Enables High‐Rate Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are promising candidates for high‐energy storage, yet their practical application is limited by poor rate capability. To date, the conversion of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) remains a major challenge due to the high energy barrier of the liquid–solid conversion from Li 2 S 4 to Li 2 S. Herein, to overcome this barrier, dibromopyrazine (DBP) was identified through screening as an effective electrolyte additive owing to its unique Br─C═N functionality, which weakens Li–S bonding via moderate Li–N coordination through the electron‐withdrawing effect of Br, thereby enabling effective LiPSs anchoring without impeding conversion. In the electrolyte containing 0.04 M DBP, the interaction favors Li 2 S 4 formation at 2.3 V and promotes three‐dimensional (3D) Li 2 S deposition. Consequently, the Li–S coin cells deliver a high capacity of 785 mAh g −1 at the high rate of 6 C and a low capacity decay rate of 0.09% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C. A 2 Ah pouch cell also demonstrates stable cycling over 100 cycles at 0.5 C. This work highlights a coordination‐modulated moderate‐interaction strategy for accelerating LiPSs conversion in Li–S batteries.

papers.title: In Situ Formed Co(OH)F Enabling Electronic and Atomic‐Level Structure Optimization in Medium‐Entropy Fluoride Cathodes for Zinc Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Cobalt‐based cathodes have attracted considerable attention in aqueous zinc batteries, however, their application remains impeded by intrinsic trade‐off between high electrochemical activity and long‐term cycling stability. Herein, an entropy‐regulated fluoride cathode is proposed to overcome the limitations via co‐engineering electronic and atomic structures. Specifically, x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and first‐principle calculations collectively demonstrate that Co(OH)F is formed in situ within the fluoride matrix during electrochemical cycling and induces electron reconstruction. Concurrently, the generated Co(OH)F shortens Co─F bond length within the entropy‐regulated fluoride, reinforcing atomic‐level structural integrity and enabling excellent cycling performance. Moreover, a hollow architecture is integrated to homogenize flux and electric field distributions, ensuring sufficient accessibility of active sites while mitigating interfacial degradation. Consequently, the assembled zinc battery exhibits a high specific capacity of 252.3 mAh·g −1 and superior cycling stability (92.4% capacity retention after 25 000 cycles at 10 A·g −1 and 90.8% capacity retention after 50 000 cycles at 20 A·g −1 ). This work demonstrates a synergistic approach that simultaneously achieves high redox activity and structural robustness in cobalt‐based cathodes for zinc batteries.

papers.title: Cathode Depolarization Enables 1300‐Cycle Ah‐Level Anode‐Free Sodium Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Nonuniform sodium deposition limits the cyclability of anode‐free sodium batteries (AFSBs), and current research mainly focuses on anode‐targeted strategies. However, the influence of the cathode kinetics on sodium deposition behavior has been overlooked. Here, we firstly reveal the critical role of cathode polarization on sodium deposition uniformity via electric field coupling. Accordingly, cathode‐specific charging (CSC) protocols are established for AFSBs to depolarize the cathode, where the charging current is dynamically regulated based on the state of charge (SOC)‐dependent direct current inner resistance (DCIR). As expected, the CSC protocols effectively depolarize the cathodes and thus homogenize sodium deposition on the anode. Impressively, a 1.6 Ah Al/C||NFPP pouch cell reaches a record‐high cyclability of 1370 cycles at 2 C, and a 3.6 Ah pouch cell reaches a high energy density of 180 Wh kg − 1 with stable cycling for 890 cycles at 0.5 C. More importantly, the cathode depolarization strategy shows application universality for diverse anode‐free full cells based on Na 4 Fe 3 (PO 4 ) 2 (NFPP), Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 (NVP), and NaNi 1/3 Fe 1/3 Mn 1/3 O 2 (NFM) cathodes. This work opens an avenue for fabricating durable practical AFSBs.

papers.title: Strengthened D‐p Orbital Hybridization Via Interlayer Coupling Enables Sulfur Redox Kinetics in Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The inherent wide bandgap and large d‐p band center energy difference (Δε d‐p ) of δ‐MnO 2 significantly impede electron transport and ion diffusion, limiting its catalytic efficiency in lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. Herein, we report an interlayer coupling strategy that intercalates cetyltrimethylammonium (CTA + ) cations into birnessite (δ‐MnO 2 ) to simultaneously modulate the Mn 3d‐O 2p orbital hybridization and expand the Li + diffusion channels. Synchrotron X‐ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy combined with density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the strong electrostatic interaction between CTA + and the MnO 2 host layers narrows the d‐p band center energy difference (Δε d‐p ) from 1.458 to 1.145 eV, substantially enhancing Mn 3d‐O 2p orbital hybridization. This optimized d‐p matching renders the Mn d‐band more compatible with the S 2p orbitals of polysulfides, synergistically optimize adsorption energies and conversion barriers. Meanwhile, the CTA + expanded interlayer afford ordered Li + diffusion channels with a high Li + transference number and uniform Li deposition. Consequently, the Li─S batteries deliver a remarkable capacity of 819.07 mAh g − 1 at 3.0 C and sustain 850 cycles at 1.0 C with an capacity decay of only 0.05% per cycle. Significantly, the Li─S pouch cell equipped with a Bir(CTAB)‐separator delivers a high energy density of 305.25 Wh kg −1 .

papers.title: Nonmetallic Anodes in Aqueous Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Rechargeable aqueous batteries are considered as promising energy storage devices due to their low cost and high safety. In rechargeable aqueous batteries, nonmetallic anodes have attracted widespread attention since they generally possess the characteristics of abundant resources, high designability, and dendrite-free. Although considerable research efforts have been made to design nonmetallic anodes, a comprehensive review about them is still absent. This review presents a systematic overview of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries, including conversion anodes and insertion anodes. Conversion-type anode materials primarily involve hydrogen gas, chalcogen compounds, and organic compounds, whereas intercalation-type anode materials focus on metal chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanionic compounds. In addition, their design principles are critically discussed with emphasis on energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations, as well as compatibility with charge carriers and cathodes. In the final section, future developments and prospects in the design of high-performance nonmetallic anodes for aqueous batteries are also discussed. It will shed light on the R&D of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries.

papers.title: Kinetic Control of Polymorphism in Li10.5Si1.5P1.5S12–Based Solid Electrolytes
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS)-type solid electrolytes (SEs) are among the most promising materials for next-generation solid-state batteries (SSBs) due to their high lithium-ion conductivity. However, challenges related to phase stability and polymorphism, especially in Ge-free, Si-based systems, limit their practical implementation. Here, the crystallization and phase transition behavior of materials with a nominal composition of Li10.5-xSi1.5P1.5S12-xIx (x = 0, 0.2, 0.4) are systematically investigated. Operando high-temperature synchrotron X-ray diffraction, total scattering with pair distribution function analysis, and differential scanning calorimetry measurements reveal the formation of a metastable orthorhombic (o) phase, followed by transformation into the thermodynamically stable tetragonal (t) phase at elevated temperatures. Our findings indicate that lithium iodide (LiI) as an additive regulates the crystallization of the o-phase and thereby governs the transition kinetics. This enables the o-to-t phase transition to occur at much reduced temperatures and faster rates. Neutron powder diffraction further uncovers minor modifications to the Si/P ratio and lithium sublattice, as well as the fact that iodine is not incorporated into the t-phase; instead, a secondary Li4PS4I-type phase forms. Collectively, this work highlights the critical role of microstructural engineering on crystallization and polymorphism in LGPS-type SEs and also demonstrates the applicability of these dual-phase materials by enabling high-performance lithium-sulfur SSBs.

papers.title: Interhalogen of Iodine Chloride Accelerates Charge Transfer for Efficient Li2O2 Oxidation in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: Li-O2 batteries suffer from sluggish Li2O2 oxidation kinetics at electrode/electrolyte interfaces, leading to large charge polarization and low energy efficiency. Soluble redox mediators (RMs) provide a solution-mediated pathway for Li2O2 decomposition and reduce the charge overpotential. However, the chemical oxidation of Li2O2 by oxidized RMs remains kinetically sluggish, resulting in persistent charge polarization. Herein, iodine monochloride (ICl), an interhalogen compound, is electrochemically generated in situ during the charge process to promote the oxidation of Li2O2. The large electronegativity difference between I and Cl promotes intramolecular charge transfer from I to Cl, creating an electrophilic iodine center (Iδ+) that increases the I-Cl bond polarity and strengthens the interaction with Li2O2. This lowers the decomposition barrier of Li2O2 from 2.39 to 0.77 eV, thereby facilitating its chemical oxidation. The Li-O2 battery delivers a low discharge/charge polarization of 0.52 V, effectively mitigating parasitic reactions at high voltages and enabling an extended cycling lifespan exceeding 800 h. This work provides a valuable design principle for developing redox mediators for efficient Li2O2 oxidation.

papers.title: Industry‐Scalable Interfacial Design for Stabilizing PET‐Cu Current Collectors
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Metallized plastic copper (Cu) current collectors (CCs), featuring a sandwich structure with polymer film—typically polyethylene terephthalate (PET)—as substrate and conductive Cu layers on both sides, offer a lighter and cheaper alternative to conventional Cu CC for lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, the instability of PET substrate in commercial carbonate electrolytes leads to Cu||PET interfacial degradation and capacity fading, particularly under high‐temperature operation. Here, we report an industry‐scalable interfacial engineering strategy to stabilize PET substrate by depositing an Al 2 O 3 layer onto the PET substrate surface via roll‐to‐roll physical evaporation (winding speed: 720 m min −1 , substrate width: 2.5 m). The conformal Al 2 O 3 coating acts as a robust physical barrier that effectively suppresses electrolyte‐induced PET substrate decomposition and maintains Cu||PET interfacial integrity during long‐term cycling. The as‐resulting Al 2 O 3 ‐coated PET‐Cu CC (PET@Al 2 O 3 ‐Cu CC) enables 3‐Ah graphite//LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 pouch cells an 86% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 45°C—comparable with the cells with commercial Cu CC (86%) and markedly superior to those using PET‐Cu CC (58%). This work establishes a low‐cost and industry‐scalable solution for stabilizing metallized plastic CCs, paving the way toward cost‐efficient and high‐energy LIBs.

papers.title: Tailoring Crystal Facets Enables Scalable Synthesis of Highly Dispersed Single Crystal NCM90
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT The single crystal cathodes show significant superiority in cycling stability and safety, but are restricted by high costs, as current preparation strategies often lead to particle agglomeration. Here, we develop a new strategy of surface high‐valence metal doping to prepare the highly dispersed single crystal LiNi 0.90 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (SC‐NCM90) in low‐cost. The surface substitution of Ni 2+/3+ by W 6+ /Mo 6+ facilitates to enhancing the bond with O, suppressing cation interdiffusion, benefiting particle dispersion, and high voltage stability. The surface Mo‐doping lowers the energy of (104) plane and stimulates its prior growth, favoring fast Li + ‐migration and endowing the Mo 6+ ‐doped SC‐NCM90 with the capacity of 111.0 mAh g −1 at 5C, achieving the desired fast charging for SC‐NCM90. W‐doping facilitates the growth of both (003) and (104) planes, benefiting the particle segregation, as (003) plane inhibits ionic fusion. W‐ and Mo‐doped SC‐NCM90 deliver markedly improved cycling life and safety performance than polycrystalline NCM90. This work establishes the strategy of high‐valence elemental surface doping as a dual‐functional paradigm that simultaneously manipulates crystal facet evolution for suppressing particle agglomeration and fortifies transition metal (TM)─O bonding for stabilizing interface, producing highly dispersed SC‐NCM90 with faster charging capability and durability.

papers.title: Elastic Graphene‐Shell Architectures Enable Stress Regulation in High‐Capacity Lithium‐Ion Battery Electrodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Silicon‐based anodes are limited by large volume changes, stress accumulation, and sluggish kinetics during cycling. Porous electrode designs can alleviate these problems, but conventional approaches often rely on multistep processing or sacrificial pore formers. Here, hollow graphene‐shell (GS) spheres are introduced as slurry‐compatible pore‐engineering additives. In a 5–60–5 MPa pressure cycle, the SiO x /GS electrode shows greater thickness recovery than pristine SiO x , with thickness‐recovery indices of 4.18 and 1.24 percentage points, respectively. Individual GS particles show a largely recoverable response within the small‐displacement range probed by atomic force microscopy (AFM), with an apparent modulus of approximately 114 MPa. Upon full lithiation, the through‐plane thickness of the SiO x /GS electrode increases by 15%, compared with 94% for pristine SiO x . The SiO x /GS electrode also retains approximately 702 mAh g −1 after 400 cycles at 1.6 A g −1 . GS improves the performance of the tested SiO x /graphite, Si@C, and LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) formulations as well. These results demonstrate a simple, slurry‐compatible strategy for accommodating electrode deformation while maintaining electrochemical performance.

papers.title: Dynamic impedance characterization of lithium-ion batteries: Experimental insights and implications for battery management
papers.abstract_en: Real-time impedance tracking holds significant potential in optimizing battery management, yet the understanding and practical utilization of dynamic impedance characteristics remain limited. In this research, a dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (DEIS) measurement protocol based on drifting-voltage suppression is developed to ensure reliable impedance extraction across various charge-discharge profiles. The DEIS measurements are performed on three cells, including a fresh NMC cell, an aged NMC cell, and a fresh LFP cell, at state of charge (SOC) levels of 80%, 50%, and 20%, and temperatures of 35, 25, and 15 °C. The results reveal two distinct dynamic impedance behaviors, which are quantitatively analyzed using the Mahalanobis distance and the coefficient of variation. Moreover, distribution-of-relaxation-time (DRT) analysis is employed to resolve relaxation features and provide qualitative insights into possible electrochemical contributions to the observed load-induced spectral distortions. Practical guidelines are provided for on-board DEIS implementation, real-time state monitoring, and dynamic impedance-based diagnosis.

papers.title: Coordination Chemistry of Single‐Atom Catalysts in Expediating Kinetics for Advanced Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
papers.abstract_en: The shuttling effect and sluggish conversion kinetics of lithium polysulfides (LiPSs) hinder the further advancement of lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries, exhibiting high barriers. Among catalysts, single-atom catalysts (SACs) can accelerate LiPSs redox kinetics by leveraging M-S coordination, interfacial charge transfer, and anchoring effect of coordinating heteroatoms. Numerous researches have reported improved catalytic activity via screening central metal and coordinating atoms as well as optimizing coordination configurations. However, systematic summary concerning the principles in screening and design of asymmetric coordination structures, the evolution mechanisms of orbital hybridization and spatial geometry, and the corresponding structure-activity relationships governing LiPSs conversion kinetics remain unknown. In this review, we systematically summarize the modifications brought by asymmetric coordination chemistry and dual-atom coordination structures in terms of geometric configuration engineering, molecular orbital hybridization, and interfacial charge rearrangement, together with the underlying mechanisms for boosting LiPSs conversion kinetics. Centered on theoretical calculations supplemented by experimental validations, we elaborate the critical significance of asymmetric coordination chemistry of SACs in elevating the catalytic efficiency. Finally, the future developments of SACs in Li─S batteries are outlooked and prospected.

papers.title: Co-doping at dual sites inducing Ni-Rich high-entropy layered oxide cathodes for high-voltage K/Na-ion storage
Charge-Density-Dependent Ionomer Effects in Pure-Water CO2 Electrolysis
papers.abstract_en: Abstract Pure-water membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) represent a promising strategy to eliminate (bi)carbonate salt precipitation for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R). However, the absence of alkali metal cations fundamentally restricts CO2 activation and intermediate stabilization, thereby reducing catalytic performance. Here, we overcome this limitation by identifying the ionomer charge density as a key molecular-level parameter associated with pure-water CO2R. By comparing anion-exchange ionomers with varying charge characteristics, we reveal that high-charge-density ionomer (HCDI) introduces a favorable catalyst–membrane interfacial environment, enabling superior macroscopic CO2R performance. HCDI-enabled MEAs achieve >99% CO Faradaic efficiency at 100 mA cm–2 and sustain ∼92% at 1000 mA cm–2. In situ diagnosis and electrochemical characterization reveal that the HCDI-functionalized interface produces a substantial *CO signal, while concurrently suppressing hydrogen evolution. By decoupling cation effects from liquid electrolytes, these findings support interfacial ionomer charge density as a useful comparative parameter for pure-water CO2 MEA electrolyzers.

papers.title: Vitamin C‐Induced Photo‐Redox Threshold Enables High‐Fidelity Volumetric Printing of Collagen
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter‐scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell–matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible‐light‐activated Ru(II)bpy 3 2+ /sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near‐immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L‐ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo‐redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high‐fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post‐printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post‐printing and cell‐laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell‐instructive 3D microenvironments.

papers.title: Rational Integration of Multiple Additives for High-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries
papers.abstract_en: Abstract The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.

papers.title: Jahn–Teller Distortion Triggers Unconventional Molecular O 2 Formation in P2‐Type Na 0.67 MnO 2 Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Oxygen redox chemistry offers a pathway to high energy density in sodium‐ion batteries but is often accompanied by irreversible molecular O 2 formation, leading to voltage hysteresis and poor cycling stability. The origin of molecular O 2 formation is commonly attributed to high‐voltage charging yet remains debatable. Here, we uncover an overlooked mechanism in P2‐type Na 0.67 MnO 2 , where molecular O 2 formation is decoupled from the conventional high‐voltage paradigm and instead originates from Jahn–Teller distortion during discharge. Combined experimental and computational results reveal that Jahn–Teller‐induced lattice distortion shortens O–O distances and enhances the O–O dimerization tendency, leading to irreversible oxygen redox and structural degradation. This finding establishes a previously unrecognized distortion‐mediated pathway governing oxygen redox. To address this issue, an Al/Si co‐doping strategy is developed to regulate the electronic structure and reinforce the lattice framework. The co‐doping suppresses Jahn–Teller distortion, stabilizes O 2p states, and weakens the tendency toward O–O dimerization, thereby inhibiting molecular O 2 formation. Consequently, the optimized Na 0.67 Al 0.01 Si 0.01 Mn 0.99 O 2 exhibits superior cycling performance, retaining 95% capacity after 100 cycles within 4.4–2.0 V and 90% after 500 cycles within 4.0–2.0 V. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for oxygen redox chemistry and offer a practical design strategy for stabilizing high‐voltage manganese‐based sodium‐ion batteries.

papers.title: Closed Pores as Internal Stress‐Regulation Units for Practical Silicon–Carbon Anodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Silicon–carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation‐induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Here, closed pores are introduced as internal stress‐regulation units to address the coupled mechanical and electrochemical instability of silicon–carbon anodes. Heteroatom‐doped carbon hosts are engineered to contain abundant closed nanopores, which redirect expansion‐induced stress toward the particle interior and suppress macroscopic electrode swelling. Meanwhile, heteroatom doping enlarges the carbon interlayer spacing and enhances electronic conductivity, enabling accelerated and more balanced Li + insertion/extraction kinetics. As a representative material, the nitrogen–doped silicon–carbon composite delivers a reversible capacity of 1756.5 mAh g − 1 , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 90.2%, and 868.4 mAh g −1 at 3 C, while reducing electrode thickness expansion from 38.4% to 13.1% after 50 cycles. The material is further produced in 6 kg batches and enables 2 Ah LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) pouch cells with 80.0% capacity retention after 1200 cycles and only 8.4% thickness growth after 900 cycles. Machine–learning–guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed‐pore design. This work establishes closed‐pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low‐expansion silicon–carbon anodes.

papers.title: Robust Sodium–Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte‐Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Sodium–metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next‐generation energy‐storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high‐concentration, localized high‐concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na + transport and generating mechanically robust, ion‐conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in‐situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine‐learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium–metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead‐sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high‐performance, practical sodium–metal batteries.

papers.title: High‐Energy and Long‐Life Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 Cathodes via Multielement V‐Site Modulation of Local M–O/F Bonding
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage, but their energy density still lags behind lithium‐ion systems. Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (NVPF) is an attractive high‐voltage polyanionic cathode, but fluorine loss generates low‐voltage Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 impurities that lower energy density and aggravate lattice deformation during cycling. Here, we report a multielement V‐site charge modulation strategy, realized in Na 3‐δ V 1.9 Zr 0.02 Ti 0.02 Cr 0.02 Fe 0.02 Al 0.02 (PO 4 ) 2 F 3 (ME‐NVPF). The deliberate combination of high‐valence Zr 4+ , Ti 4+ , and same‐valence Cr 3+ , Fe 3+ , Al 3+ cations creates a heterogeneous M–O/F bonding network with multi‐directional electrostatic interactions enhancing lattice‐F retention that completely eliminates NVP impurities, lowers the Na + migration barrier, and reduces unit‐cell volume variation to merely 2.87%. Consequently, ME‐NVPF delivers a record‐high energy density of 477 Wh kg −1 , sustains 11 000 cycles, operates across −40 to 80°C, and is further validated in 600 mAh‐level pouch cells. This work establishes multielement compositional regulation as an effective strategy for designing high‐energy, long‐life, and all‐temperature polyanionic cathodes.

papers.title: Activation‐Induced Turbostratic Ordering in pDCPD‐Derived Hard Carbon Enables Stable Carbonate‐Based Sodium‐Ion Storage
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Sodium–ion batteries are widely considered a promising alternative to lithium‐ion batteries, due to the abundance and low cost of their raw materials. However, the development of high‐performance and cost‐effective electrode materials remains a significant challenge, particularly when competing with lithium iron phosphate systems. Herein, we present a hard carbon material derived from readily available poly(dicyclopentadiene) for use as a negative electrode in SIBs. This study investigates the influence of carbonization temperature and subsequent activation on the hard carbon structure and electrochemical performance. The impact of activation proved to be dependent upon the first stage carbonization temperature, creating greater local ordering for samples carbonized at higher temperatures. The removal of defects and increase in interlayer distance resulted in a turbostratic structure that enhanced rate performance and capacity retention when compared with non‐activated samples. The optimized hard carbon exhibits a reversible capacity of 352 mAh at 0.1 C and a capacity retention of 88.1% after 500 cycles with a carbonate based electrolyte. This work introduces a cost‐effective approach for producing hard carbon materials with distinctive nanostructure and provides valuable insights into achieving long cycle life in sodium–ion batteries.

papers.title: Reliable performance evaluation and mechanistic characterization of aqueous zinc batteries: From laboratory testing to practical applications
Spatially Decoupled Charge Compensation Enables Versatile Cation–Anion Co‐Intercalation in Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Multivalent cation–anion co‐(de)intercalation offers a promising pathway to higher energy densities in multivalent ion batteries. However, its practical realization is challenged by lattice strain and the lack of effective dual charge‐compensation strategies. Here, we report a layered vanadium oxide cathode with pre‐intercalated melamine ligands (MeVO) that enables a spatially decoupled charge‐compensation mechanism—organic ligands serve as redox centers for anions, while metal sites accommodate multivalent cation redox. This design alleviates electrostatic crowding, promotes ion mobility, and preserves structural integrity. Using Mg 2 + ‐TFSI − as a representative system, MeVO delivers a record cycle life of over 36 000 cycles at a loading of approximately 3 mg cm − 2 and an areal capacity of 3.3 mAh cm − 2 at a higher loading of 16.4 mg cm − 2 , surpassing leading Mg‐ion cathodes. The hybrid structure also supports co‐(de)intercalation of various multivalent cations and anions, demonstrating its potential as a versatile intercalation platform for high‐performance energy storage.

papers.title: Phase‐Selective NiCo Oxide Electrodes Enable Paired Electrochemical Conversion and Valorization of Nitrogen‐Containing Wastewaters
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Conventional wastewater treatment generally focuses on pollutant removal while consuming energy and recovering little chemical value. Here, we report a phase‐selective Ni‐Co oxide platform for paired electrochemical conversion of nitrogen‐containing contaminants, coupling cathodic acetonitrile (AN) hydrogenation to ethylamine (EA) with anodic hydrazine oxidation to N 2 . Annealing NiCo layered double hydroxide precursor under Ar and in air produces cubic NiCoO 2 and spinel NiCo 2 O 4 , respectively, which exhibit complementary catalytic preferences. NiCoO 2 achieves 90.4%–91.2% Faradaic efficiency toward EA over 50–200 mA cm −2 in 8 wt.% AN, whereas NiCo 2 O 4 approaches 100% Faradaic efficiency toward N 2 over the same current‐density range. Combined in situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that this catalytic complementarity arises from phase‐dependent reaction energetics: NiCoO 2 favors H‐assisted AN hydrogenation while enabling facile EA release, whereas NiCo 2 O 4 promotes hydrazine dehydrogenation and, critically, N 2 desorption and active‐site regeneration. A 100 cm 2 membrane‐electrode assembly maintains 88–93% EA Faradaic efficiency and stable paired operation for 120 h. The paired system was further demonstrated using separately collected industrial wastewaters, together with downstream EA recovery and a preliminary process‐level assessment. These results establish crystal‐phase regulation of reaction and product‐release energetics as a strategy for matching distinct electrode reactions within paired wastewater valorization.

papers.title: A High-Nickel Cathode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries Integrating a Proposed 3D Ionic Percolation Network and Interwoven Layered/Rock-Salt Nanodomains
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract_en: High-nickel single-crystal cathodes effectively address the poor mechanical stability and severe side reactions that plague their polycrystalline counterparts. However, they introduce new structural challenges, including extended Li+ diffusion pathways, which in turn lead to structural slips, lattice distortions, and phase transformations, ultimately compromising both electrochemical capacity and structural stability. Herein, we report a state-of-the-art cathode architecture for high-nickel materials, derived from high-energy neutron irradiation of single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2 particles. This process induces long-range Li/Ni antisite disorder and short-range metal-oxygen octahedral distortions, concurrently yielding a nanostructure of abundant grain boundaries and interwoven layered/rock-salt nanodomains within the single-crystalline particles. These grain boundaries are proposed to constitute a 3D percolation network for rapid Li+ transport, whereas the interwoven nanodomains may act as local structural reinforcing units that help suppress irreversible phase transitions and the propagation of interfacial side reactions during cycling. These characteristics are favorable for sustaining continuous Li+ deintercalation/intercalation and reversible electrochemistry, thereby preserving the structural stability of the single-crystal framework while simultaneously shortening diffusion pathways. As a result, the engineered cathode delivers a high specific discharge capacity of 213.9 mAh/g at 0.2 C and 152.2 mAh/g at 10 C (within 4.5 V). Moreover, it retains 80.0% of its initial capacity after 450 cycles at 5 C, significantly outperforming the reference single-crystal cathode (64.2%). This work establishes high-energy neutron irradiation as an effective cathode reconstruction strategy, offering a viable route toward robust, high-energy cathodes.

papers.title: Stress Regulation through Precursor Chemistry: From Synthesis to Cycling Stability in O3‐Type Layered Oxide Cathodes
papers.abstract_en: ABSTRACT Layered oxide cathode materials have broad application prospects in sodium‐ion batteries. However, conventional oxide solid‐state synthesis route, transition metal oxides slowly participate in the reaction step by step, causing residual stress accumulation and cycling degradation. Herein, a synthesis strategy utilizing low‐melting‐point metal salt precursors is proposed. Leveraging their synchronous decomposition and liquid‐like characteristics, a uniform chemical environment is generated, fundamentally suppressing the uneven accumulation of residual stress. Thermal analysis and kinetic calculations demonstrated that the reaction activation energy of the metal salt system (NFM‐A) was significantly reduced and exhibited a more stable variation profile. This effectively circumvented the asynchronous reaction process caused by diffusion kinetic differences inherent to the traditional oxide route (NFM‐O). Multiple experimental characterizations consistently confirmed that the residual stress of NFM‐A was low and uniformly distributed. After prolonged cycling, NFM‐A maintained a uniform lattice strain distribution with complete and dense particle morphology, while continuous stress concentration, interlayer slip, and particle cracking occurred in NFM‐O. Combined with in situ XRD and finite element simulations, the critical role of the initial stress distribution in maintaining structural integrity during electrochemical cycling is revealed. This establishes stress regulation as a key criterion for designing layered oxide cathode materials with high structural stability.
